data.title: Solar eclipse 2026: Africa witnesses partial eclipse
data.description:
Part of the world turned its eyes to the skies this Wednesday.

The eclipse was also visible across Africa. In Tabarka, where the phenomenon was most pronounced in Tunisia, 59.06% of the Sun was obscured.

The partial eclipse was also visible from Dakar and several regions of Senegal, with a maximum of around 37% of the Sun's disk obscured towards the end of the day.

And to make sure they didn't miss the celestial event, our correspondents in Tunisia and Senegal also put on their special eclipse glasses.

data.title: Ukrainian cathedrals, Gaza’s archives, Iranian squares – modern war is systematically erasing human history | Simon Jenkins
data.description: It is not enough now for war to kill, it must eradicate a people’s cherished and precious heritage too Wars may not take summer holidays, but they do sometimes see exhaustion. As drones race back and forth across Ukraine and the strait of Hormuz, a grim stalemate seems to have invaded the earth beneath. Aerial bombardment knows limited resistance and even less victory or defeat. Ukraine, Russia, Israel, Iran and their allies seem able to defy diplomacy and drop bombs on each other for ever. At which point the outside world can merely count some of the costs. Vladimir Putin’s known desire to eliminate Ukraine’s historical identity has led to its cultural devastation. Two weeks ago Unesco reported the destruction or dereliction of 545 of its historic buildings, including 156 religious sites and 43 museums. The attempted eradication of what Putin himself claims to be an intrinsic part of Russia’s own history is sickening. Simon Jenkins is a Guardian columnist Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.title: ‘It was lonely being a young queer artist’: Sam Smith on finding health, happiness – and their hazel-eyed fiance
data.description: On their new album, Smith is subverting their singer-songwriter roots to tell a queer love story. They talk about their shifting fanbase, the nasty undercurrents of fame – and finding sanctuary in New York City Sam Smith logs on to our video call with the username “Lily of the Valley”, the May-born singer’s birth flower. It sets a serene tone. They’re in Guadalajara, Mexico, for the latest stop of a residency tour, titled To Be Free, in support of their fifth studio album. Instead of Smith’s usual jet-lagged arena itinerary, this lower-key excursion stops at smaller venues in only six cities and sheds the ostentatious theatricality of their last outing. On stage on their last tour, “I was flailing around on a massive gold bum and had, like, seven costume changes,” Smith says with a chuckle. It’s intimacy they’re after now, the ability to satisfy their “craving to look at people again”, which matches the romantic feeling of their fifth album, Hazel Eyes. But for Smith, whose genre-shifting stardom has been accompanied by harsh controversies, it’s also a chance to observe who’s still in their corner: “There’s some wonderful people that have stayed, but it’s a completely different room than it was with In the Lonely Hour,” their 2014 debut. Continue reading...

data.title: Will Trump’s next press secretary be a better liar than the first five?
data.description: As Karoline Leavitt plans to step down, it’s apparent how the president above all values a readiness to twist the truth As Karoline Leavitt prepares to step down from her role as Donald Trump ’s fifth White House press secretary, a brief review of her tenure , and that of her predecessors, makes clear that the most fabulist president in US history prizes one quality above all else in the women and men who speak for him: a willingness to tell outrageous lies. Leavitt started her tenure by telling a wild falsehood at her very first news conference, when she claimed that the Biden administration had planned to use $50m in taxpayer dollars to send condoms to Gaza. Later the same day, the Guardian reported that the claim was directly contradicted by USAID records. Continue reading...

data.title: Experience: I found my long-lost twin aged 49
data.description: The joy, disbelief and shock of discovering I had a brother the same age as me came with a million questions. How were we separated and why? In 1975, my parents saw an advert in their local Australian newspaper. With the Vietnam war coming to an end, thousands of orphaned children were being evacuated. As part of the American-led Operation Babylift, the Australian government was looking for families who would adopt them. My parents decided to do it. I arrived in Adelaide in April in a shoebox. I was so tiny that my umbilical cord was still attached. My parents knew that the document they were given, with a January birthday and the name Le Thi Ha, couldn’t be mine. But with the chaos of the evacuation there was no way to find out more. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘So much more respect for myself’: NZ ultrarunner Sophie Woods on smashing a 2,000km alpine run record
data.description: Sophie Woods speaks about the challenges she overcame while completing the notorious Via Alpina across eight European countries A couple of weeks into her record-breaking 2,000km run through Europe’s alps, Sophie Woods feared she might die. Woods and her photographer had just scaled a peak in Switzerland, when a severe thunderstorm engulfed them. “The lightning was going off around us ... there was nowhere to shelter in place [and] all the rocks around us were conductive,” Woods tells the Guardian, from her home in Andorra, nearly two weeks after she became the fastest person ever to run the Via Alpina, a 2,000km network of alpine trails through eight countries. data.title: My friend’s negative self-talk is straining our relationship. What can I do? | Leading questions
data.description: Self-doubt doesn’t respond to evidence, writes advice columnist Eleanor Gordon-Smith . Rather than disputing it, perhaps you could engage in a different way Read more Leading questions A close friend of mine is suffering with crippling self-doubt and it’s starting to take a strain on our relationship. We’ve been friends for eight years. She is such a bright, bubbly and charismatic person who has an infectious ability to make people laugh and feel welcome; but she also has a really low opinion of herself and, as her friend, I am the one who always gets the brunt of her negative self-talk. After every social event she will message me to ask if I think she has annoyed someone, or that she spoke too much, or that she embarrassed herself. In private conversations she is constantly putting herself down, calling herself fat, apologising for nothing and generally claiming she’s not good enough. I love her and constantly reassure her that her thoughts have no grounding but, after years of this, I am tired. I’m starting to enjoy our time together less and less, as I never know what mood she will be in or what she will say about herself. I would hate to hear anyone else speak about her in the way she does. I especially hate it when she says these things about herself. Continue reading...

data.title: The Schoolgirl Terrorist? review – by the end of this documentary you feel like you have sat through a nightmare
data.description: A vulnerable girl took her life at 16 having faced terror charges and online grooming by neo-fascists. The catalogue of failures by British authorities is utterly enraging The Schoolgirl Terrorist? contains its answer within its very question. Titles are designed to catch your attention. Normally they contain the baldest, most extreme possible summary suggestion of what you are about to see that the makers think they can get away with. A question mark introduces the idea of interrogation, of nuance, of doubt from the off – all things commissioners believe will put people off. data.title: ‘It was fun to get pushed around’: Andrew Rannells on ‘razzle dazzle’, kissing co-stars and being a better friend to Lena Dunham
data.description: The star of Girls and The Book of Mormon talks about coming out, turning a showmance into a romance, and going toe to toe with the West Wing’s Allison Janney in new film Miss You Love You Imagine a cute, young, gay Jim Carrey with a withering line in put-downs: that is Andrew Rannells. Or rather, it was, back when he starred in Lena Dunham’s HBO series Girls as Elijah, the formerly closeted ex of her character, Hannah. Dunham had seen Rannells playing Elder Price, the zealous missionary spreading the good word in the original 2011 Broadway production of the bad-taste musical The Book of Mormon , for which he received a Tony nomination. Girls, in turn, spread the good word about him. To this day, fans still shout “Your dad is gay!” at him in the street, a call-back to the moment when Elijah tartly advises Hannah that she might want to fine-tune her gaydar. It is an older, gentler, salt-and-pepper-bearded Rannells who stars in the comedy-drama Miss You, Love You . He plays Jamie, a personal assistant arriving in Albuquerque, New Mexico, to shepherd the spiky and recently widowed Diane ( Allison Janney) through the initial weeks after her husband’s death from Parkinson’s. As it dawns on them that Diane’s son – Jamie’s employer – may not make it to his stepfather’s funeral, these strangers navigate their way through the grey area of their flung-together friendship. Continue reading...

data.title: Burnham won’t fix our prisons crisis until he dares to be honest with the public about crime | Polly Toynbee
data.description: Most crime figures have drastically fallen, but people don’t believe it. It’s no wonder when politicians whip up emotions and attempt to bend the law An astounding change is happening to life in England and Wales that most people don’t know about, and when they are told they don’t believe it. Most crime, including violence, has fallen by a remarkable 90% over the past 30 years. But only 6% of people believe it, while 61% think crime is going up . This great denial is the background cause of the prison overflow crisis, as politicians (of all parties) stir up voters to demand ever higher sentences as the imaginary cure to their imaginary soaring crime. All western European countries enjoy this same remarkable social improvement, with research over decades offering myriad reasons why: populations spending longer in education, CCTV, better security for cars and homes, and young people staying at home to play video games of fantasy crime instead of entertaining themselves with the real thing. Removing brain-harming lead from petrol and abortion of unwanted foetuses at risk of future child neglect are other possible explanations. Polly Toynbee is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

data.title: The Jason Arday affair must not spell the end for diversity. Here’s how – and why – we should defend it | Joseph Harker
data.description: The scandal has given succour to the same old rightwing attacks on D&I, but companies that do it properly raise standards rather than lowering them This has not been a good fortnight for the concept of diversity and inclusion. The fallout from the Jason Arday affair has been an all-out attack, by the rightwing media and political classes, on institutional efforts to reduce inequality. Arday was the Black academic who, in a fanfare of publicity, had been appointed a professor at Cambridge University in 2023. At the time, British institutions were still struggling to address the widespread issues of systemic racism thrown up by the murder of George Floyd three years earlier. data.title: AOC’s public egg-freezing shouldn’t feel radical. But in today’s US, it does | Moira Donegan
data.description: The congresswoman’s decision is an assertion of women’s freedom and dignity at a time when our status is rapidly eroding “Don’t be weird about this,” Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, the progressive star and rumored 2028 presidential contender, said on her live video broadcast as she raised her shirt to angle the syringe into her abdomen. Then, with resignation, “even though I know all of you will be.” The New York Democrat is 36 years old, and this week she revealed that she is beginning the process of freezing her eggs during Congress’s August recess. In the video, Ocasio-Cortez said that she was seeking to destigmatize the realities of women’s lives as they navigate the conflicting demands of professional aspiration and family building; she explained to viewers the process of the hormonal injections she was administering to herself, showing them the drugs and injector she was using arrayed on a paper towel, beside a disinfecting towelette. The procedure, Ocasio-Cortez explained, was not covered by her insurance, and she would be paying “100% out of pocket”. She had been saving to afford it for some time. “This is a choice that I am making to feel more in control of my life,” she said, going on to assert her hope that transparency about such questions will destigmatize women’s reproductive lives and promote their dignity. Continue reading...

data.title: Taylor Swift has put her love story out there – so it’s not fair she won’t let us see her wedding dress | Polly Hudson
data.description: How a bride decides to look on the big day tells us a lot about that person. But the singer is leaving us hanging Having hope in your heart is all well and good, but you also need to know when to give up. At a certain point it’s time to accept cold, hard reality: we’re never going to see pictures of Taylor Swift in her wedding dress, are we? There are many reasons this matters, and the first, admittedly, is plain old nosiness, with a side order of entitlement. We’ve spent years absorbing – some unintentionally, by osmosis – the details of Swift’s relationships, following her journey to happily ever after every step of the way, including the photos she released of the engagement moment. Obviously she is allowed to keep her wedding private, but being denied a glimpse of the dress feels – insert foot stamp here – unfair. More than that, it’s like a romcom ending before the final embrace, the protagonist still en route to the airport they have yet to run through. For somebody who is essentially a storyteller, this tale is uncharacteristically incomplete, unsatisfying. It’s not like Swift to leave us hanging. data.title: The Guardian view on solar eclipses: moments of wonder that bring us together | Editorial
data.description: Wednesday’s eerie spectacle united crowds beneath the sky, continuing a human fascination that stretches from ancient myth to modern physics “I’d describe it as a magical eeriness.” Lisa Redfern’s description to the Guardian conveys the combination of beauty and wrongness that accompanied Wednesday’s partial solar eclipse in Britain. Crowds across the country assembled as the sun’s power seemed to wane, twilight changed tone abruptly, the temperature fell and the familiar landscape took on an unnatural appearance. In a divided world, there is comfort in coming together in awe. Ms Redfern, speaking from Cornwall, was right that Britons “may not see another one. We have to make the most of these moments.” The country has to wait 55 years for another comparably deep partial eclipse. To experience the true marvel of the eclipse, one had to be in the path of totality – which this week crossed over Greenland, Iceland and Spain. There the sun was completely obscured. Britain saw a partial version, with the moon covering part of the sun, with only a thin yellow crescent showing. Totality is another world of wonder: for a few minutes a black disc appears where the sun should be, surrounded by a fiery corona in a purplish firmament. It is 64 years before a total eclipse of the sun will be seen over Britain. Continue reading...

data.title: Championship spending hits record levels and likely to go higher as playoffs expand
data.description: With a top-eight finish offering at least a playoff place, the temptation to spend big in pursuit of the Premier League will grow – but so will the risks The Championship’s collective wage bill grew to a record £903m in 2024-25, according to Deloitte’s latest Annual Review of Football Finance. Clubs are paying players enormous sums in their pursuit of Premier League football. With the playoffs expanding this season , the number of owners willing to risk even more money in the hope of securing promotion is only likely to increase. In isolation, the figure of £903m does not signify much. Compared to the Premier League’s £4.4bn salary outlay, it almost looks small. But England’s top division can afford that gargantuan commitment to wages whereas the second tier cannot. The 24 clubs in the Championship earned £942m, meaning salaries consumed 96% of revenue. If there was any surprise in their collective net debt being £1.4bn at the end of 2024-25, it was only that it had reduced from the £1.5bn it was a year earlier. Continue reading...

data.title: Jack Draper ‘in difficult place’ after defeat by Martín Landaluce at Cincinnati Open
data.description: Former world No 4 slumps to 6-3, 7-5 first-round loss Draper still recovering from long-term arm injury The minuscule amount of confidence and self-belief Jack Draper currently has to call upon in the most difficult period of his career was underscored in the first game of his opening match in Cincinnati. Draper began his service game by shanking a forehand into the back fence, which he followed up with two double faults. He immediately fell down a break and never recovered. A few fleeting positive moments followed, but this miserable start set the tone for another excruciating day for the former world No 4 as he could not escape the mental fatigue borne out of battling serious injury for 15 months and counting. Draper fell 6-3, 7-5 to Martín Landaluce, the world No 64. Continue reading...

data.title: Nearly 100 children detained as adults under UK-France migration deal
data.description: Figures emerge in critical letter to Home Office from organisation appointed to scrutinise detention facilities Nearly 100 children have been wrongly identified and detained as adults under Shabana Mahmood’s “one in, one out” deal with France, the Guardian can disclose. Home Office staff said that of 304 age-disputed cases arising from the scheme over nine months, 94 (31%) – were ultimately found to be minors. Children are supposed to be excluded from the scheme, while government policy limits immigration detention of unaccompanied children to 24 hours. Had been awaiting deportation for more than six months, despite being supposed be held for up to 28 days only “in exceptional cases”. Were being readied for removal to France despite having TB or requiring hospital treatment. Faced removal after being separated from family members with whom they had travelled, which she said had a “particularly damaging impact”. Continue reading...

data.title: From toxic blooms to dead zones, how wildfires transform oceans and lakes
data.description: Wildfire smoke and ash can reshape aquatic ecosystems long after the flames have been extinguished Wildfires are an increasing problem in Europe and elsewhere. While their immediate effect on air quality is obvious, they can also trigger less visible but significant environmental effects, including algal blooms. An algal bloom is the rapid growth of algae and other plant-like microorganisms. These blooms can become so dense that they change the colour of the lake and seas. Although most are harmless, some produce dangerous toxins. When their blooms die, their decomposition depletes oxygen in the water, creating so-called dead zones. Continue reading...

data.title: Wing and a prayer: how probiotics might save bat species from a killer fungus
data.description: Bat experts were shocked at how fast white-nose syndrome had spread to Canada’s northernmost colonies from the US. Now, the race is on to find a cure before species disappear Crawling through a narrow passage in a cave beneath a boreal forest near Fort Smith in Canada’s Northwest Territories in May, two biologists spotted a lifeless bat on a limestone ledge, its body covered in a spindly white fungus. When they shone their headlamps to get a closer look, they saw another bat with the fungus on its forearms. “It hissed at us and crawled back into a crack,” Jesika Reimer says. Continue reading...

data.title: DRC’s fast-growing Ebola outbreak spreads to sixth province
data.description: Man dies in Bas-Uele after travelling from Haut-Uele, as head of WHO says outbreak on track to be deadliest ever The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has spread to a sixth province, officials have said, a day after the head of the World Health Organization said the outbreak was on track to surpass the deadliest in history, which killed at least 11,000 people more than a decade ago. The current outbreak has killed more than 2,100 people out of more than 4,500 cases, according to the latest government figures released on Tuesday. At the same point in the 2014-16 outbreak in west Africa, the previous most deadly outbreak, 755 cases had been recorded, according to WHO data. Continue reading...

data.title: Dear Michelle Kwan review – fire and ice in a whirlwind figure-skating comedy
data.description: theSpace Triplex, Edinburgh Four skaters enter into feral competition in this darkly funny yet flimsily plotted play about female teenhood The title refers to the figure-skating legend and Olympian who, in the noughties, captivated the US with her performances on ice, winning a total of five world championships. Here, the four teen skaters trying to make it big worship her, quite literally, invoking her for strength on and off the ice. It is a great central idea with moments of frozen action as each girl sends a wish, a fear or prayer up to a godlike, absent Kwan in their most anxious or exhilarated moments. Christie Spessard’s play has verve, capturing the extremes of adolescent life and competitive sport. Energetically directed by Ryan Pangracs, it is full of humour with some zingers and movement that contains a true sense of gliding. At theSpace Triplex, Edinburgh , until 29 August All our Edinburgh festival reviews Continue reading...

data.title: My Brilliant Career review – a joyous heroine lights up this rare and beautiful period drama
data.description: Phillipa Northeast is brilliant as a young woman rebelling against society’s expectations in 1890s Australia. It is witty, intelligent and absolutely glorious to watch “I’m hot headed, with a snub nose, and that’s why I prefer a direct gaze.” So speaks Sybylla, the charmingly irrepressible and irrepressibly charming heroine of My Brilliant Career, played utterly convincingly and with vim, vigour and joy by Philippa Northeast in the new adaptation of Miles Franklin’s 1901 Australian classic of the same name. Creator Liz Doran must have wept with happiness when they found an actor capable of bringing so much to an already glorious script – and who embodies the joie de vivre upon which so much of the plot, as everyone she meets becomes part of her orbit, depends. My Brilliant Career is on Netflix Continue reading...

data.title: The End of Tom Six review – Human Centipede director delivers one last freaky flick
data.description: Now living with multiple sclerosis, Six rants about the masturbation film distributors won’t touch and the money mystery behind his horror hit Fifteen years ago, Dutch film-maker Tom Six succeeded where almost everybody fails – particularly in the world of horror. He actually shocked people. No self-respecting sophisticate admits to being shocked, of course, and no horror connoisseur will admit to being really and truly horrified. But Six really did freak audiences out with his extreme exploitation nightmare The Human Centipede, the first of a trilogy. It was a grenade in the faces of prim conformists, and also those badass horror fans who thought they’d seen it all. The “human centipede” of the title is created by a sadistic surgeon who imprisons three young people in a basement and sews them together mouth-to-anus as a vivisectional experiment. Six himself had been a director on the original Dutch TV show Big Brother that started the global franchise, and it was easy to see how his movie masterwork was intended as a satire on consumerist voyeurism and cruelty. Or maybe it just sprang from the same dark creative place that gave birth to the TV phenomenon of the age. Continue reading...

data.title: Bruckner Symphony No 3 album review – Anima Eterna’s period instruments bring visceral drama
data.description: Anima Eterna Brugge/Heras-Casado (Harmonia Mundi) There’s bone-crushing intensity in this striking recording of the original version of the Bruckner’s third. Pablo Heras-Casado teases out vital, almost operatic detail According to legend, in the summer of 1873 Anton Bruckner travelled to Bayreuth intending to dedicate one of a pair of scores to his hero, Wagner. Apparently, the two composers got legless and by the time Bruckner arrived back home, he could no longer remember which symphony the master preferred. In a flap, he put pen to paper: “Symphony in D Minor, where the trumpet begins the theme?” he fished. “Yes! Best wishes! Richard Wagner,” was the reply. With its mighty peaks and faint reminiscences of the operas, the Wagnerian aesthetic looms large over the Third Symphony in D minor, especially in its more radical original version, presented here by period instrument specialists Anima Eterna . Gut strings and original woodwind and brass are more pungent than their modern counterparts, but they sometimes struggle to summon the weight necessary for Bruckner. Not here. Pablo Heras-Casado conducts one of the most explosive and visceral accounts on record with his Belgian orchestra laying into the score with bone-crushing intensity. Continue reading...

data.title: Universality by Natasha Brown audiobook review – a sparkling multi-voiced satire
data.description: A magazine article about stolen gold sparks a culture war between a cast of politically polarised characters A stinging dissection of wealth, class and the media, Natasha Brown’s satire begins with a man named Jake gazing at a gold bar he has found at a farm in West Yorkshire. Outside, an illegal rave is taking place which will end in three hospitalisations and property damage. Pondering what to do with the ingot that he has just used to bludgeon a stranger, Jake decides to do a runner. The story of the stolen gold is told by a journalist, Hannah, in a magazine article named A Fool’s Gold, replicated in full here, which she claims exposes “the fraying fabric of British society, worn thin by late capitalism’s relentless abrasion”. Her piece, which goes viral, features Richard Spencer, an arrogant, philandering banker and the owner of the farm, whose reputation is left in tatters; a contrarian rightwing newspaper columnist named Miriam Leonard, known as Lenny; and a group of radical anarchist squatters who call themselves The Universalists. Continue reading...

data.title: Chelsea Wolfe: The Dark review – existential reflection goes from whisper to gothic scream
data.description: (Loma Vista) The genre-blending Californian artist casts off past toxic influences with a powerful set of tender, brooding and emotionally charged songs that wouldn’t feel out of place as festival anthems When Chelsea Wolfe was interviewed by the Guardian in 2015 about her fourth album, Abyss, she revealed that her music had been informed by the bouts of sleep paralysis she’d suffered from since childhood. The condition – a transitional state between being awake and asleep – affects sufferers in different ways. Some wake up feeling paralysed, others see ghosts or demonic figures. For the California-born singer-songwriter, it meant “waking up, and you can move your body and your eyes are open, but there are figures and people from your dreams still present in your room”. No surprise, then, that her music – a blend of drone, alt, folk, industrial and doom metal – had ended up so spookily unsettling. She appeared on album covers with pupil-less eyes, spoke in interviews about “following the path of witchcraft” and even covered Norwegian black metal act and convicted arsonist/murderer Burzum. She did have a sense of humour about it all, however, telling one interviewer, with a chuckle: “It’s not party music.” Since then, though, much has changed. Wolfe left Los Angeles for the mountains above the city – where she’s finally been able to enjoy a good night’s sleep. Sobriety since 2021 has also brought what she calls “a new clarity”. Both developments inform The Dark. Continue reading...

data.title: Can Nothing Save Us? by Irvine Welsh review – US family saga is a late-career triumph
data.description: The Scottish author focuses on gun culture and generational conflict in this darkly satirical tale about a great power in decline “Why expect unconditional love from somebody you’ve brought into a fucked, dying planet, who then has to sit around and watch you screw it up even more?” So muses twentysomething college dropout Luke Ayrton on his parental lineage as he works the Las Vegas Strip, “comping girls for clubs” in Sin City. His job is to trawl the “plankton” of bacherlorette parties in order to lure the “whales” – rich men willing to spend to try to impress young women. “In this game your sociology skills sharpened,” it’s observed, but beyond the seedy side hustle lie weightier concerns: the matter of his family legacy. Electronic dance music aficionado and aspiring writer Luke is estranged from his Maga-positive Mom and Dad, and now lives with grandparents George and Molly, affluent boomers with a countercultural past. data.title: Agent 64: Spies Never Die review – licence to kill time like the 90s never ended
data.description: PC; Replicant D6 This GoldenEye 007-styled retro shooter is an agreeable set of straightahead shooting missions that hark back to a simpler time, with simpler controls With 007 First Light , 2026 has already given us the best James Bond game in more than three decades, since the release of Rare’s N64 classic GoldenEye 007. But what about those players whose loyalties lie not with the super-spy himself but the particulars of that 90s interpretation of his adventures? Enter Agent 64: Spies Never Die. Made almost entirely by a single developer (who goes by the very cloak-and-dagger alias Replicant D6), its production values couldn’t be much further from the blockbuster First Light. data.title: ‘I feel like I’m at war’: are we losing the battle against machine-made music?
data.description: Despite outcry from musicians, AI slop is creeping into the charts as record labels scramble to adapt to a new normal where hits can be made at the click of a button This year, the battle for song of the summer has been eclipsed by a much more complicated – some would even say disturbing – debate. That’s because we find ourselves asking not “What’s the song of the summer?” but rather “Is the song of the summer even real ?” Among the top contenders for the title is Fenix Flexin’s Rubberz , a single released in June that has ascended to No 58 on the Billboard Hot 100 and racked up more than 35m Spotify streams. It’s not the sort of fare Fenix usually cooks up. The artist is known for his trap music as part of the rap duo Shoreline Mafia, but Rubberz is a mildly noirish, 80s-inspired synth-pop track featuring a voice nothing like his. The song has drawn comparisons to Morrissey, but it more closely resembles Men at Work’s Down Under, or a Weird Al Yankovic parody of Men at Work. It’s pretty awful. But more importantly, it has an uncanny quality to it. It sounds off. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I wanted to capture the range of British culture at the time’: the photographer who documented late nights on the 90s London tube
data.description: In the 1990s, Mark McEvoy took portraits of punks, partiers and late-night lovers on the underground. His images show city life before smartphones – when people still had to rush to make the final train Mark McEvoy’s tube photographs, taken in London Underground carriages at around 11pm on Friday and Saturday nights from 1992 to 1995, capture moments that may seem superficially frivolous, but might be the most significant of our lives. These are the golden hours of the end of the week, where friendships are found and sealed; gabbled conversation rolls along with the sway of the carriages; and new lovers meet up en route for an encounter that may turn out to be a fleeting one-off, or in fact the beginnings of a lifelong companionship. All are swept along in the scramble to hop onboard the last tube – a panic that ended when all-night services began on some lines 10 years ago this month. The night tube arrived when my time of going out all weekend was fading, and gave me a slight feeling of missing out. Looking at photos of other people’s social lives can make one feel like that too; at the same time, it’s not hard to see ourselves in these tired, happy and thoughtful faces. Continue reading...

data.title: Helen Goh’s recipe for frozen Eton mess with plum, coconut and raspberry | The sweet spot
data.description: The classic British dessert, but with a frozen twist, captures all of the charm of the original with a welcome chill for summer I love the glorious unruliness of Eton mess, all billowy cream, crushed meringue and tumbling fruit. This frozen version captures all of that charm but in a sliceable, make-ahead dessert that’s perfect for August entertaining. The fruit can even be cooked a day in advance, leaving little more to do than whip everything together before freezing. Thanks to the condensed milk, the cream freezes surprisingly softly, while the meringue keeps its gentle chew and the toasted coconut adds a welcome crunch and nuttiness. Late summer plums bring a lovely tartness that balances the sweetness beautifully, though apricots, peaches and nectarines would also work well. Continue reading...

data.title: Berries with a hint of tarmac – what do we mean when we call a wine ‘fruity’?
data.description: Bananas, peaches, strawberries – anything but ‘grapes’. What do all those volatile organic compounds really mean for your summer sipping? “Strawberries, cherries and an angel’s kiss in spring,” sang Nancy Sinatra . “My summer wine is really made from all these things …” Overlook the angel’s kiss and, if you’re a wine drinker, you might recognise some of those fruity tasting notes – strawberries and cherries, indeed, but also citrus, orchard, other stone fruits and the whole berry family. In fact, it’s common to liken a wine to almost any fruit – except grapes. A wine can have notes of almost anything – pencil shavings, tennis balls, cat pee – but fruit is the most obvious (clearly, wine is made from fruit) and universally recognised. If I told you I was getting, say, green apple and lime zest from a riesling, you would probably have a good sense of what that meant, and what you might be able to expect on tasting it yourself. If I described a petroleum aroma, that might sound a bit cryptic and much less appealing, unless you were familiar with this tasting note commonly found in riesling. In other words, a wine’s fruit profile is often leveraged as a marketing tool. What better example of this than the “strawberries and cream” of Provence rosé? It’s a tasting note that underpins our collective sense that rosé is a summer drop, perfect for sun-drenched days filled with watching tennis, ocean views and seasonal produce. Continue reading...

data.title: Escaping the ​heat​ and rediscovering the ​joy of ​cooking
data.description: Parts of the UK are roasting but some of us are glad to turn the oven on. Bring on the​ ​curries and pasta pies Sign up here for our weekly food newsletter, Feast I don’t wish to boast, but I’m typing this with a jumper on. Not because my flat has air-conditioning, but because it doesn’t – and the relentless heat of south-east England was having a seriously detrimental effect on my productivity and the health of my elderly dog (NB: the two are not mutually exclusive). So, with a second novel to write , I decided to rent a studio as far north, and as far west, as I could reasonably drive in a day. And, so far, I have no regrets. Driving through North Yorkshire, I had to put on a sweatshirt – the weather in the Pennines gave my car the first good wash it’s had in months – and now, in Scotland, the dog and I feast on hot porridge in the mornings. I’d genuinely forgotten what it’s like to be cold – and what it’s like to cook for pleasure. This newsletter isn’t just for those parts of the country enjoying, rather than suffering, the sunshine; yesterday it was raining and tonight the temperatures will drop to almost single digits. It’s also for anyone, wherever you are, who’s eaten enough cool, crunchy salads and chilled soups to last a lifetime, or at least until next summer. (You’re not alone: last month, Waitrose reported a spike in sales of cottage pie and robust South African red wine.) Continue reading...

data.title: What is the MMR vaccine and how does Trump’s executive order affect parents and children?
data.description: President’s order calls for several changes to childhood vaccinations – and experts say it’ll lead to confusion On Monday, Donald Trump signed an executive order pushing for revisions to how children in the US are vaccinated. The executive order calls for several changes. These include fewer vaccinations overall and a recommendation that the combined measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine be replaced with separate shots for each disease administered during separate medical visits. The latter direction is currently impossible to implement because no stand-alone shots for these diseases are licensed in the US. Continue reading...

data.translatedTitle: After more than eight months at sea, living conditions on board the aircraft carrier “Abraham-Lincoln” are worrying
data.translatedDescription: Democratic elected officials are demanding explanations after reports of shortages, health problems and a deterioration of mental health on board the ship. The specialized media “Navy Times” reports that two sailors attempted suicide by throwing themselves overboard.

data.title: Aujourd’hui, l’Occupation est peu abordée par un théâtre pourtant prompt à s’emparer des sujets politiques
data.description: « Le théâtre sous l’Occupation » (5/5). Ariane Mnouchkine, Julien Gosselin, Stanislas Nordey ou Jeanne Balibar goûtent peu les œuvres créées à Paris durant la guerre. Mais la période incite à se poser une question : que faire si l’extrême droite arrive au pouvoir en 2027 ?
data.translatedTitle: Today, the Occupation is rarely addressed by a theater that is quick to take on political subjects
data.translatedDescription: “The theater under the Occupation” (5/5). Ariane Mnouchkine, Julien Gosselin, Stanislas Nordey or Jeanne Balibar had little taste for the works created in Paris during the war. But the period prompts a question: what if the far right comes to power in 2027?

data.title: Aux Etats-Unis, trois condamnés à mort exécutés dans la même journée dans trois Etats différents
data.description: Le fait que ces trois injections létales aient eu lieu le même jour est une coïncidence mais cela reflète le rythme soutenu des exécutions aux États-Unis où, depuis le début de l’année, 22 condamnés à mort ont subi la peine capitale.
data.translatedTitle: In the United States, three death row inmates executed on the same day in three different states
data.translatedDescription: The fact that these three lethal injections took place on the same day is a coincidence but it reflects the sustained pace of executions in the United States where, since the start of the year, 22 death row inmates have received the death penalty.

data.title: Au Brésil, la police remet la main sur des œuvres d’Henri Matisse volées en 2025 à Sao Paulo
data.description: Les œuvres, estimées à environ 200 000 dollars par la police, faisaient partie d’un ensemble de treize illustrations dérobées en décembre dans la bibliothèque Mario de Andrade, au cœur de la plus grande ville du pays.
data.translatedTitle: In Brazil, police recover works by Henri Matisse stolen in 2025 in Sao Paulo
data.translatedDescription: The works, estimated at around $200,000 by police, were part of a set of thirteen illustrations stolen in December from the Mario de Andrade library, in the heart of the country's largest city.

data.title: Au Japon, des pluies diluviennes font au moins quatre morts à l’est de Tokyo
data.description: Les précipitations ont fortement perturbé les réseaux routier et ferroviaire et bloqué des milliers de personnes à l’aéroport international de Narita, qui dessert la capitale.
data.translatedTitle: In Japan, torrential rains kill at least four people east of Tokyo
data.translatedDescription: The precipitation severely disrupted road and rail networks and stranded thousands of people at Narita International Airport, which serves the capital.

data.title: Yann Vézilier, l’agent de la DGSE condamné au Mali à vingt ans de prison, a été gracié
data.description: Après un an de détention, Yann Vézilier, qui était dûment accrédité comme officier de la direction générale de la sécurité extérieure auprès des autorités maliennes, a été gracié jeudi par le chef de la junte, le général Assimi Goïta. Une libération obtenue au terme de plusieurs mois de tractations diplomatiques.
data.translatedTitle: Yann Vézilier, the DGSE agent sentenced in Mali to twenty years in prison, was pardoned
data.translatedDescription: After a year of detention, Yann Vézilier, who was duly accredited as an officer of the general directorate of external security to the Malian authorities, was pardoned Thursday by the head of the junta, General Assimi Goïta. A release obtained after several months of diplomatic negotiations.

data.title: Adieu « fake news », bonjour « FIMI » : le lexique de la désinformation fait peau neuve
data.description: « Dix ans de post-vérité » (4/5). A peine Donald Trump élu en 2016, l’anglicisme « fake news » se diffuse dans le monde entier. Ambigu, malmené et récupéré, il est aujourd’hui remplacé par des termes plus techniques.
data.translatedTitle: Goodbye “fake news”, hello “FIMI”: the lexicon of disinformation gets a makeover
data.translatedDescription: “Ten Years of Post-Truth” (4/5). As soon as Donald Trump was elected in 2016, the anglicism “fake news” spread throughout the world. Ambiguous, mishandled and recovered, it is today replaced by more technical terms.

data.title: Hürtgenwald: Waldbrand in der Eifel – NRW-Ortsteil evakuiert
data.description: Die Feuerwehr kämpft gegen einen Waldbrand im nordrhein-westfälischen Kreis Düren. Weil die Flammen einem Teil der Gemeinde Hürtgenwald gefährlich nahekommen, müssen sich nun Hunderte Menschen in Sicherheit bringen.
data.translatedTitle: Hürtgenwald: Forest fire in the Eifel – NRW district evacuated
data.translatedDescription: The fire brigade is fighting a forest fire in the Düren district in North Rhine-Westphalia. Because the flames are coming dangerously close to part of the Hürtgenwald community, hundreds of people now have to get to safety.

data.title: News: Frust in der SPD, Bandengewalt in Berlin, Futtermangel in der Landwirtschaft
data.description: Die SPD-Chefs ziehen den Zorn der Basis auf sich. Eine Serie von Schutzgelderpressungen erschüttert Berlin. Landwirten geht das Tierfutter aus. Das ist die Lage am Freitagmorgen.
data.translatedTitle: News: Frustration in the SPD, gang violence in Berlin, lack of feed in agriculture
data.translatedDescription: The SPD leaders are drawing the wrath of the rank and file. A series of protection rackets shakes Berlin. Farmers are running out of animal feed. This is the situation on Friday morning.

data.title: SPD-Rentenexpertin schlägt Abschaffung der »Rente mit 63« in fünf Jahren vor
data.description: Teile von SPD und CDU rebellieren gegen die geplante Abschaffung der Frührente. Nun meldet sich die linke SPD-Politikerin Annika Klose zu Wort. Sie hat die Reform mit verhandelt und schlägt nun eine Übergangsfrist vor.
data.translatedTitle: SPD pension expert proposes abolishing the “pension at 63” in five years
data.translatedDescription: Parts of the SPD and CDU are rebelling against the planned abolition of early retirement. Now the left-wing SPD politician Annika Klose speaks out. She helped negotiate the reform and is now proposing a transition period.

data.title: Dürre und Hitzewelle: Bauernverband befürchtet in einigen Regionen »totalen Ernteausfall«
data.description: Hitze und Trockenheit haben Folgen für die Landwirtschaft: Vor allem in Süddeutschland dürfte die Ernte schlecht ausfallen, warnt der Bauernverband und fordert von der Regierung Hilfen und billigeren Agrardiesel für Landwirte.
data.translatedTitle: Drought and heat wave: Farmers' association fears "total crop failure" in some regions
data.translatedDescription: Heat and drought have consequences for agriculture: the harvest is likely to be poor, especially in southern Germany, warns the farmers' association and is calling on the government to provide aid and cheaper agricultural diesel for farmers.

data.title: Ulrich Siegmund und die AfD in Sachsen-Anhalt: Der gefährlichste Mann Deutschlands
data.description: AfD-Spitzenpolitiker Ulrich Siegmund will sich in Sachsen-Anhalt an die Macht lächeln. Hinter ihm: ein rechtsextremes Netzwerk und Personal, das selbst der eigenen Parteispitze Angst macht. Die SPIEGEL-Titelstory.
data.translatedTitle: Ulrich Siegmund and the AfD in Saxony-Anhalt: The most dangerous man in Germany
data.translatedDescription: AfD top politician Ulrich Siegmund wants to smile his way to power in Saxony-Anhalt. Behind him: a right-wing extremist network and staff that even scares his own party leadership. The SPIEGEL cover story.

data.title: Lettland: Kampfjets fangen Drohne ab
data.description: Über dem lettischen Luftraum haben Nato-Jets eine Drohne bisher unbekannter Herkunft abgeschossen. Zuvor waren Anwohner aufgerufen, sich in Sicherheit zu bringen. Auch Finnland hat Vorsichtsmaßnahmen ergriffen.
data.translatedTitle: Latvia: Fighter jets intercept drone
data.translatedDescription: NATO jets shot down a drone of previously unknown origin over Latvian airspace. Previously, residents were asked to get to safety. Finland has also taken precautionary measures.

data.title: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez: Linke Ikone mit wachsenden Präsidentschaftsambitionen
data.description: Sie ist der Star bei den Demokratischen Sozialisten: Die Abgeordnete Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez bereitet sich auf höhere Ämter vor. Und verärgert dabei ihre linken Weggefährten.
data.translatedTitle: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez: Left-wing icon with growing presidential ambitions
data.translatedDescription: She is the star of the Democratic Socialists: Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez is preparing for higher office. And in the process annoys her left-wing companions.

data.title: Kennedy Center: Donald Trumps Name soll an Fassade zurückkehren
data.description: Die Posse um das Kennedy Center in Washington geht in die nächste Runde: Donald Trump besteht weiter darauf, dass sein Name das Kulturzentrum ziert. Ein Gericht lehnte das ab – nun will das Zentrum zu einem Trick greifen.
data.translatedTitle: Kennedy Center: Donald Trump's name should return to the facade
data.translatedDescription: The farce surrounding the Kennedy Center in Washington is entering the next round: Donald Trump continues to insist that his name adorn the cultural center. A court rejected this - now the center wants to resort to a trick.

data.title: Nach Klagen über Missstände: US-Flugzeugträger wird abgelöst
data.description: Schimmlige Duschen und eine halbe Tasse Reis mit zwei Tortillas zum Essen: Die US-Marine reagiert auf Berichte über die Missstände auf dem Flugzeugträger »USS Abraham Lincoln«. Eine Ablösung ist wohl schon auf dem Weg.
data.translatedTitle: After complaints about grievances: US aircraft carrier is being replaced
data.translatedDescription: Moldy showers and half a cup of rice with two tortillas to eat: The US Navy reacts to reports of abuses on the aircraft carrier “USS Abraham Lincoln”. A replacement is probably already on the way.

data.title: Donald Trump ordnet Rückkehr zu Dampfkatapulten auf US-Flugzeugträgern an
data.description: Der US-Präsident hat selbst nie in der US-Armee gedient – aber zu Militärthemen trotzdem immer eine klare Meinung. Aktuell im Fokus: Flugzeugträger. Trumps jüngste Anordnung dürfte Milliarden kosten.
data.translatedTitle: Donald Trump orders return to steam catapults on US aircraft carriers
data.translatedDescription: The US President never served in the US Army himself - but still has a clear opinion on military issues. Currently in focus: aircraft carriers. Trump's latest order is expected to cost billions.

data.title: Ukrainekrieg: Schwerer russischer Bombenangriff auf Kramatorsk
data.description: Russland hat die frontnahe Stadt Kramatorsk in der Ostukraine erneut mehrfach aus der Luft angegriffen. Die Ukraine meldet mindestens einen Toten und mehrere Verletzte. Anwohnern wird geraten, umzusiedeln.
data.translatedTitle: Ukrainian War: Heavy Russian bombing of Kramatorsk
data.translatedDescription: Russia has again attacked the city of Kramatorsk in eastern Ukraine, which is close to the front line, from the air several times. Ukraine reports at least one death and several injuries. Residents are advised to relocate.

data.title: Block-Prozess: Entführte Kinder laut Psychiaterin traumatisiert
data.description: Sie wurden in der Silvesternacht von Dänemark nach Deutschland entführt, mutmaßlich im Auftrag ihrer Mutter. Nun hat eine Sachverständige mögliche Folgen für die Kinder der Unternehmerin Christina Block dargelegt.
data.translatedTitle: Block trial: kidnapped children traumatized according to psychiatrist
data.translatedDescription: They were kidnapped from Denmark to Germany on New Year's Eve, presumably on behalf of their mother. Now an expert has explained possible consequences for the children of entrepreneur Christina Block.

data.title: Erling Haaland: Polizei stellt Kokain mit Konterfei des Fußball-Stars sicher
data.description: Sei es auf dem Fußballplatz oder in den sozialen Medien: Erling Haaland ist derzeit omnipräsent. Fahnder in Ecuador haben sein Konterfei nun aber an einem ungewöhnlichen Ort ausgemacht.
data.translatedTitle: Erling Haaland: Police seize cocaine with a portrait of the football star
data.translatedDescription: Be it on the football field or on social media: Erling Haaland is currently omnipresent. Investigators in Ecuador have now located his portrait in an unusual location.

data.title: USA vollstrecken drei Todesurteile an einem Tag in Tennessee, Oklahoma und Alabama
data.description: Unter der Trump-Regierung sind US-Bundesstaaten angehalten, verurteilte Mörder hinzurichten. Und viele folgen dieser Direktive eifrig: Zuletzt gleich dreimal binnen 24 Stunden.
data.translatedTitle: USA carries out three death sentences in one day in Tennessee, Oklahoma and Alabama
data.translatedDescription: Under the Trump administration, US states are required to execute convicted murderers. And many follow this directive eagerly: most recently three times within 24 hours.

data.title: US-Zölle von Donald Trump: Importierte Drohnen sollen bis zu 100 Prozent teurer werden
data.description: Mit neuen Zöllen wollen die USA die Abhängigkeit von chinesischen Drohnenherstellern verringern und die heimische Produktion stärken. Durch die Maßnahme könnten auch zwei Söhne des US-Präsidenten profitieren.
data.translatedTitle: US tariffs from Donald Trump: Imported drones should become up to 100 percent more expensive
data.translatedDescription: With new tariffs, the USA wants to reduce dependence on Chinese drone manufacturers and strengthen domestic production. Two sons of the US President could also benefit from the measure.

data.title: Tirol: Deutscher Wanderer stürzt bei Familienausflug in den Tod
data.description: Ein Mann ist mit Schwiegervater und Schwägern in den Zillertaler Alpen unterwegs. Plötzlich verliert er das Gleichgewicht und stürzt in die Tiefe. Die anderen Männer versuchen, ihn zu retten – vergeblich.
data.translatedTitle: Tyrol: German hiker falls to his death on a family trip
data.translatedDescription: A man is traveling with his father-in-law and brothers-in-law in the Zillertal Alps. Suddenly he loses his balance and falls into the depths. The other men try to save him - in vain.

data.title: Leichtathletik-EM: Leo Neugebauer holt EM-Gold im Zehnkampf – Niklas Kaul Zweiter
data.description: Der Weltmeister triumphiert auch bei der EM: Leo Neugebauer hat sich im Zehnkampf gegen seinen Teamkollegen Niklas Kaul durchgesetzt. Am Ende reichten 38 Punkte Vorsprung.
data.translatedTitle: European Athletics Championships: Leo Neugebauer wins European Championship gold in the decathlon – Niklas Kaul second
data.translatedDescription: The world champion also triumphed at the European Championships: Leo Neugebauer prevailed in the decathlon against his teammate Niklas Kaul. In the end, a 38-point lead was enough.

data.title: Leichtathletik-EM: Gesa Krause gewinnt Gold über 3.000 Meter Hindernis
data.description: In einem dramatischen Finale über 3000 Meter Hindernis hat Gesa Krause das erste EM-Gold für Deutschland geholt – und den dritten EM-Triumph ihrer Karriere. Olivia Gürth gewann Bronze, Lea Meyer stürzt.
data.translatedTitle: European Athletics Championships: Gesa Krause wins gold in the 3,000 meter obstacle
data.translatedDescription: In a dramatic final over the 3000 meter steeplechase, Gesa Krause won Germany's first European Championship gold - and the third European Championship triumph of her career. Olivia Gürth won bronze, Lea Meyer falls.

data.title: Hamburg: Zehntausende Zeugen Jehovas feiern Gottesdienst im Volksparkstation
data.description: 2023 wurden in Hamburg sieben Zeugen Jehovas von einem früheren Mitgläubigen getötet. An diesem Wochenende treffen sich Zehntausende der Fundamentalisten in der Stadt. Können sie das Trauma von damals überwinden?
data.translatedTitle: Hamburg: Tens of thousands of Jehovah's Witnesses celebrate church service in the Volksparkstation
data.translatedDescription: In 2023, seven Jehovah's Witnesses were killed in Hamburg by a former fellow believer. This weekend tens of thousands of fundamentalists will meet in the city. Can they overcome the trauma from back then?

data.title: Kim Cattrall wird 70
data.description: Die Erfolgsserie »Sex and the City« machte Kim Cattrall zum Star, aber das hatte nicht nur positive Folgen. Jetzt wird Cattrall 70 Jahre alt – und hat Samantha Jones längst hinter sich gelassen.
data.translatedTitle: Kim Cattrall wird 70
data.translatedDescription: The hit series "Sex and the City" made Kim Cattrall a star, but it didn't only have positive consequences. Now Cattrall is 70 years old – and has long since left Samantha Jones behind.

data.title: Flughafen Leipzig/Halle: Sprengstoffdrohne legt deutsche Verwundbarkeit offen
data.description: Der Leipziger Flughafen entging nur knapp einer Katastrophe. Der versuchte Anschlag mit einer Sprengstoffdrohne zeigt, wie verwundbar Deutschland ist. Die Behörden haben nach SPIEGEL-Informationen inzwischen kaum mehr Zweifel: Hinter der Attacke dürfte Moskau stecken.
data.translatedTitle: Leipzig/Halle Airport: Explosive drone exposes German vulnerability
data.translatedDescription: Leipzig Airport narrowly escaped disaster. The attempted attack with an explosive drone shows how vulnerable Germany is. According to SPIEGEL information, the authorities now have little doubt: Moscow was probably behind the attack.

data.title: Sachsen-Anhalt: CDU-Kandidat Sven Schulze, zwei Wahlplakate und ein Fauxpas
data.description: Spott und Häme für Sven Schulze, den Spitzenkandidaten der CDU in Sachsen-Anhalt: Zwei seiner Wahlplakate zeigen dieselbe »Frau aus dem Volk«, allerdings mal im Rollstuhl, mal nicht. Peinliche Panne oder gängige Praxis?
data.translatedTitle: Saxony-Anhalt: CDU candidate Sven Schulze, two election posters and a faux pas
data.translatedDescription: Mockery and malice for Sven Schulze, the CDU's top candidate in Saxony-Anhalt: two of his election posters show the same "woman of the people", although sometimes in a wheelchair, sometimes not. Embarrassing glitch or common practice?

data.title: Thüringen: Sahra Wagenknecht lehnt Björn Höckes Wahlangebot ab und fordert TV-Duell
data.description: AfD-Politiker Björn Höcke will Sahra Wagenknecht zur Ministerpräsidentin Thüringens wählen. Die schlägt das Angebot aus und macht einen Gegenvorschlag.

data.translatedDescription: AfD politician Björn Höcke wants to elect Sahra Wagenknecht as Prime Minister of Thuringia. She rejects the offer and makes a counterproposal.

data.title: Chineses vêm ao Brasil em busca de 30% do mercado de biotecnologia
data.description: "A solução definitiva para salvaguardar a segurança alimentar está em aprimorar a ciência e a tecnologia." A frase é de Xi Jinping, presidente chinês, e reflete a preocupação do país com o abastecimento alimentar. Empresas e governo da China vêm atuando fortemente nessa direção, com velocidade na execução de planos e volumosos investimentos. Por onde se passa, são aparentes os sinais dessa revolução. Assim como fizeram com a indústria, principalmente com a automobilística, os chineses agora querem fazer o mesmo com a agricultura . Leia mais (08/13/2026 - 23h00)

The phrase is from Xi Jinping, Chinese president, and reflects the country's concern with food supply. Chinese companies and the government have been acting strongly in this direction, with speed in executing plans and voluminous investments. Everywhere you go, the signs of this revolution are apparent. Just as they did with industry, especially automobiles, the Chinese now want to do the same with agriculture. data.translatedTitle: Mysterious "zombie salmon" in Torne River: "Just want to cry"
data.translatedDescription: NISKANPÄÄ Leif Taavola and Tore Peuravaara see sick salmon almost every day. The fish wander around, deprived of their natural instincts. When they die, they later float to the surface. Why do salmon in Torneälven become "zombies"? - We are ready to cry, says Leif Taavola, recreational fisherman in the area.

data.translatedTitle: The heat broke Hansson: "I felt completely shaken"
data.translatedDescription: PARIS. Louise Hansson continues to search for the form that has escaped. The swimmer who won EC gold four years ago, and who two years ago took WC bronze and was in the Olympic final, did not make it to the EC final in the 100 meter butterfly. data.translatedTitle: S on handling the notebook: "It's embarrassing"

data.title: Lars Calmfors: Partiernas löften är så svajiga att det knappt går att räkna på dem
data.description: Socialdemokraterna tar inte med sin bankskatt när de räknar på effekterna av sina förslag. Och Moderaterna hävdar att de kan skaka fram 70 miljarder kronor i besparingar genom effektiviseringar, utan andra bevis än ett par powerpointbilder. Det är omöjligt för väljarna att bedöma realismen i de siffror som slängs runt i valrörelsen. KOLUMNEN. Lars Calmfors är professor emeritus i internationell ekonomi, forskare vid IFN och fristående kolumnist på Dagens Nyheters ledarsida.
data.translatedTitle: Lars Calmfors: The parties' promises are so shaky that it is hardly possible to count on them
data.translatedDescription: The Social Democrats do not include their bank tax when calculating the effects of their proposals. And the Moderates claim that they can generate SEK 70 billion in savings through efficiency improvements, with no other evidence than a couple of PowerPoint slides. It is impossible for voters to judge the realism of the numbers thrown around in the election campaign. THE COLUMN. Lars Calmfors is professor emeritus in international economics, researcher at IFN and independent columnist on Dagens Nyheter's editorial page.

data.title: DN Debatt. ”Många år i Sverige räcker inte för att bli integrerad”
data.description: DN DEBATT. Var femte migrant som bott i Sverige i över två decennier har aldrig förvärvsarbetat. Tid i landet är inte det avgörande, utan det krävs faktiska möten med det svenska samhället och svenskfödda. Därför bör språkstudier inom SFI i mycket större utsträckning kombineras med konkret samhällsorientering, skriver forskningsledaren Bi Puranen vid World values survey.
data.translatedTitle: DN Debate. "Many years in Sweden are not enough to become integrated"
data.translatedDescription: DN DEBATE. Every fifth migrant who has lived in Sweden for over two decades has never worked gainfully. Time in the country is not the decisive factor, but actual meetings with Swedish society and those born in Sweden are required. Therefore, language studies within SFI should be combined to a much greater extent with concrete social orientation, writes research leader Bi Puranen at the World values ​​survey.

During Thursday, the rescue service was back in the area and investigated the accident scene.

data.title: IF Metall avbryter strejken mot Tesla
data.description: Fackföreningen IF Metall avbryter strejken mot Tesla. Det multinationella fordonsbolaget uppges ha köpt ut IF Metalls strejkande medlemmar. – Utan strejkande finns ingen strejk, säger Veli-Pekka Säikkälä, avtalssekreterare på LO.
data.translatedTitle: IF Metall calls off the strike against Tesla
data.translatedDescription: The union IF Metall calls off the strike against Tesla. The multinational vehicle company is said to have bought out IF Metall's striking members. - Without strikers there is no strike, says Veli-Pekka Säikkälä, contract secretary at LO.

data.title: David Ritschard inviger festivalen med värme och hjärta
data.description: David Ritschard förknippas ofta med Stockholms södra förorter, men hans musik kan inte avfärdas som en regional angelägenhet. På Way out west i Göteborg står han för en sympatisk och musikaliskt skicklig timme, skriver Gabriel Zetterström.
data.translatedTitle: David Ritschard opens the festival with warmth and heart
data.translatedDescription: David Ritschard is often associated with Stockholm's southern suburbs, but his music cannot be dismissed as a regional affair. At Way out west in Gothenburg, he represents a likeable and musically skilled hour, writes Gabriel Zetterström.

data.title: Demenssjuk engelsman utvisas på grund av brexit
data.description: George Mason, 74, har svår demens och behöver vård dygnet runt. Nu har den brittiske medborgaren en vecka på sig att lämna Sverige – efter 25 år i landet. – Sveriges migrationspolitik väger tyngre än min pappas hälsa. Det är omänskligt, säger sonen Carl Mason.
data.translatedTitle: Englishman with dementia is deported because of Brexit
data.translatedDescription: George Mason, 74, has severe dementia and needs round-the-clock care. Now the British citizen has one week to leave Sweden - after 25 years in the country. - Sweden's migration policy weighs more heavily than my father's health. It's inhumane, says son Carl Mason.

data.translatedTitle: False health advertisements on the Internet cause patients to drop vital medicines

data.translatedTitle: Anyone who reads this and is human is in the minority
data.translatedDescription: Recently, people have become a minority online. More than half of internet traffic comes from robots. And that means that the revenue model of many companies has to be overhauled, because AI visitors do not generate advertising money.

data.description: Hij was een van de invloedrijkste politici uit de recente geschiedenis. De oorlog en Jodenvervolging bleven Jacques Wallage zijn hele leven bezighouden. Hij overleed woensdag op 79-jarige leeftijd.

data.translatedDescription: He was one of the most influential politicians in recent history. The war and the persecution of the Jews continued to occupy Jacques Wallage throughout his life. He died on Wednesday at the age of 79.

data.title: In de strijd om Groenlandse olie zoekt een Amerikaans bedrijf de mazen van de wet op: ‘Een soort arctische stunt’
data.description: Het Amerikaanse bedrijf Greenland Energy wilde in oktober olie gaan boren in Groenland en heeft het eerste materiaal al aan land gebracht. Het heeft alleen geen toestemming en krijgt die voorlopig ook niet.
data.translatedTitle: In the battle for Greenlandic oil, an American company is looking for loopholes: 'A kind of Arctic stunt'
data.translatedDescription: The American company Greenland Energy wanted to drill oil in Greenland in October and has already landed the first material. It just doesn't have permission and won't get it for the time being.

data.title: Wat te doen tegen droogte? Water beter vasthouden, strijden tegen verzilting, soms overlast accepteren maar vooral: ‘veel steviger klimaatbeleid’
data.description: Overal worden noodmaatregelen genomen tegen de droogte. Er zijn wel plannen voor ‘droogtemanagement’, maar die zijn vaak nog in een experimentele fase. Nederland moet anders leren omgaan met water. „We zien dat de meest extreme scenario’s met betrekking tot klimaatverandering al eerder realiteit zijn.”
data.translatedTitle: What to do about drought? Retain water better, fight against salinization, sometimes accept nuisance, but above all: 'much stronger climate policy'
data.translatedDescription: Emergency measures are being taken everywhere against the drought. There are plans for 'drought management', but they are often still in an experimental phase. The Netherlands must learn to deal with water differently. “We see that the most extreme scenarios regarding climate change have already become reality.”

data.title: Oud-politicus en voormalig burgemeester van Groningen Jacques Wallage (79) overleden

data.translatedTitle: Former politician and former mayor of Groningen Jacques Wallage (79) has died
data.translatedDescription: Wallage was mayor of Groningen for more than ten years. He also led the PvdA's House of Representatives faction in the late 1990s.

data.title: Tanker uit Russische schaduwvloot lekt olie bij kust van Oman, mogelijk grootste olieramp in jaren
data.description: De tanker had zo’n 800.000 vaten internationaal gesanctioneerde Russische olie aan boord toen op 6 juni een „incident” buiten Omaanse territoriale wateren plaatsvond. De olie verspreidt zich in een gebied met kwetsbare ecosystemen.
data.translatedTitle: Tanker from Russian shadow fleet leaks oil off Oman coast, possibly biggest oil spill in years
data.translatedDescription: The tanker was carrying some 800,000 barrels of internationally sanctioned Russian oil when an "incident" occurred outside Omani territorial waters on June 6. The oil spreads in an area with fragile ecosystems.

data.translatedTitle: Trump taken to court over paid offering of information through Truth Social
data.translatedDescription: The Freedom of the Press Foundation and news site The Intercept have sued Donald Trump before a federal judge.

data.title: Het Nederlandse voetbal loopt als een rode draad door Xavi’s carrière – als creatieve coach moet hij zich nog bewijzen
data.description: Met de verrassende aanstelling van Xavi Hernández als bondscoach gaat de KNVB voor aanvallend en creatief voetbal. Voetbal waarmee Xavi als speler tot grote prestaties kwam, maar dat hij als trainer nog weinig heeft laten zien.
data.translatedTitle: Dutch football runs like a common thread through Xavi's career - he still has to prove himself as a creative coach
data.translatedDescription: With the surprising appointment of Xavi Hernández as national coach, the KNVB is opting for attacking and creative football. Football with which Xavi achieved great results as a player, but which he has not yet shown much as a trainer.

data.title: Kapotte camera’s, munten, speelgoed – bij Vintage.com krijgen ze dagelijks duizend dozen met ‘oude troep’ binnen. Wat er precies in zit, is elke keer een verrassing
data.description: Vintage.com in Duiven krijgt dagelijks een stortvloed aan dozen te verwerken. Die bevatten ‘oude troep’ uit kelders, zolders en opslagboxen. Het personeel opent ze, bekijkt de inhoud en taxeert de waarde. Gemiddeld ligt die tussen de 100 en 200 euro.
data.translatedTitle: Broken cameras, coins, toys – Vintage.com receives a thousand boxes of 'old junk' every day. What exactly is in it is a surprise every time
data.translatedDescription: Vintage.com in Duiven deals with a flood of boxes every day. These contain 'old junk' from cellars, attics and storage boxes. The staff opens them, examines the contents and assesses the value. On average it is between 100 and 200 euros.

data.title: Niets moet, alles mag: tijdens introductieweken bepalen studenten zelf of ze alcohol drinken. ‘Al hoort het d’r wel een beetje bij’
data.description: Terwijl de Gezondheidsraad adviseert om alcoholgebruik te denormaliseren en te ontmoedigen, schuwen veel studenten het niet om tijdens studentenintroductiedagen te drinken. Intussen proberen de organiserende partijen dat te ontmoedigen. „Natuurlijk bieden we fris goedkoper aan dan alcohol.”
data.translatedTitle: Nothing is mandatory, everything is allowed: during introductory weeks, students decide for themselves whether they drink alcohol. 'Although it is a bit part of it'
data.translatedDescription: While the Health Council advises to denormalize and discourage alcohol use, many students do not shy away from drinking during student introduction days. In the meantime, the organizing parties are trying to discourage this. “Of course we offer soft drinks cheaper than alcohol.”

data.title: Mislukte aanslag op Oekraïens vrachtvliegtuig in Leipzig vormt nieuwe stap in hybride oorlogvoering: ‘Dit was de eerste gewapende aanval met een drone in Duitsland’
data.description: Voor het eerst werd vorige week in Duitsland een gewapende aanval met een drone gepleegd. De Duitse regering reageert voorzichtig. ‘Maar als je niet reageert op dit soort aanvallen, is dat een uitnodiging om het vaker te doen.’
data.translatedTitle: Failed attack on Ukrainian cargo plane in Leipzig marks a new step in hybrid warfare: 'This was the first armed attack with a drone in Germany'
data.translatedDescription: An armed drone attack was carried out for the first time in Germany last week. The German government is reacting cautiously. “But if you don't respond to these types of attacks, it's an invitation to do it more often.”

data.title: Nieuwe wetgeving voor zorgorganisaties moet ‘hackers het zo lastig mogelijk maken’
data.description: De nieuwe Cyberbeveiligingswet verplicht grote zorgorganisaties tot verhoogde digitale weerbaarheid. Op 15 augustus gaat de wet in. Bestuurders krijgen meer verantwoordelijkheid, ook voor hun leveranciers. Toezichthouders krijgen „extra opties om de druk op te voeren”, maar beloven „niet meteen met boetes te gaan zwaaien”.
data.translatedTitle: New legislation for healthcare organizations should 'make it as difficult as possible for hackers'
data.translatedDescription: The new Cybersecurity Act obliges large healthcare organizations to increase digital resilience. The law will come into effect on August 15. Directors are given more responsibility, also for their suppliers. Supervisors will be given "additional options to increase the pressure", but promise "not to immediately start waving fines".

data.title: In derde expositie ‘Artists against the Kremlin’ protesteren Russische kunstenaars wederom tegen de oorlog in Oekraïne
data.description: Masha Trebukova is een van de vele Russische kunstenaars die exposeren in de expositie ‘Artists against the Kremlin’ in De Balie. In 1990 verruilde zij Moskou voor Amsterdam. Na de Russische inval in Oekraïne kon ze een tijdlang geen kwast oppakken. „Rusland is zo trots op haar cultuur, maar richt tegelijkertijd dit aan.”
data.translatedTitle: In the third exhibition 'Artists against the Kremlin', Russian artists once again protest against the war in Ukraine
data.translatedDescription: Masha Trebukova is one of the many Russian artists exhibiting in the exhibition 'Artists against the Kremlin' in De Balie. In 1990 she exchanged Moscow for Amsterdam. After the Russian invasion of Ukraine, she was unable to pick up a brush for a while. “Russia is so proud of its culture, but at the same time it is doing this.”

data.title: Klimaatgerelateerde schade neemt toe, daar moeten klanten zich beter op voorbereiden, zegt grote verzekeraar
data.description: Achmea’s halfjaarcijfers vielen lager uit door de onweers- en hagelschade van afgelopen juni. De klimaatverandering stelt de verzekeraar voor grote uitdagingen.
data.translatedTitle: Climate-related damage is increasing, customers must be better prepared for this, says a major insurer
data.translatedDescription: Achmea's half-year figures were lower due to the thunderstorm and hail damage last June. Climate change poses major challenges for insurers.

data.title: Wie de Japanse vlag onteert, riskeert straks twee jaar gevangenis, maar kunstenaar Aida laat zich niet tegenhouden
data.description: Het beschadigen van Japans nationale vlag is vanaf deze donderdag strafbaar. Deskundigen noemen het symboolpolitiek, maar waarschuwen toch voor zelfcensuur. „Ik dacht: wat zijn ze nu weer voor een belachelijke wet aan het maken?”
data.translatedTitle: Anyone who dishonors the Japanese flag will soon risk two years in prison, but artist Aida will not be stopped
data.translatedDescription: Damaging Japan's national flag will be punishable from this Thursday. Experts call it symbolic politics, but still warn against self-censorship. “I thought: what kind of ridiculous law are they making?”

data.title: Ik durf het bijna niet te zeggen, maar we leven steeds gezonder
data.description: Rosanne Hertzberger durft het bijna niet op te schrijven, maar: we leven steeds gezonder en daardoor worden we minder vaak ziek.
data.translatedTitle: I hardly dare to say it, but we are living increasingly healthier lives
data.translatedDescription: Rosanne Hertzberger hardly dares to write it down, but: we live healthier lives and therefore we get sick less often.

data.title: Als die ene collega dienst had, kwam ze ’s nachts naar het werk
data.description: Een vrouw werkt als zorgassistent in een verpleeghuis. Haar werk gebeurt overdag. Toch gaat ze ook vaak ’s nachts naar het werk. Omdat ze de bewoners zo mist? Of omdat die ene collega dan werkt? De kantonrechter stemt in met ontslag op staande voet. De vrouw gaat in hoger beroep.
data.translatedTitle: When that one colleague was on duty, she came to work at night
data.translatedDescription: A woman works as a care assistant in a nursing home. Her work happens during the day. Yet she often goes to work at night. Because she misses the residents so much? Or because that one colleague works? The subdistrict court judge agrees to summary dismissal. The woman appeals.

data.title: Uniek moment: Rob Trip op het dak
data.description: Woensdagavond was een avond vol beelden die de tv-recensent nooit zal vergeten. Met een zonsverduistering, Rob Trip op het dak en livestreams. „Zit jij ook de NOS Livestream te kijken?”
data.translatedTitle: Unique moment: Rob Trip on the roof
data.translatedDescription: Wednesday evening was an evening full of images that the TV critic will never forget. With a solar eclipse, Rob Trip on the roof and live streams. “Are you also watching the NOS Livestream?”

data.title: In Azië draaide WOII om een afrekening met het Europees imperialisme
data.description: Historicus Hans van de Ven schrijft in zijn nieuwe boek dat het Westen de geopolitieke ontwikkelingen heeft onderschat die de Tweede Wereldoorlog in Azië in gang zette. Het belang daarvan verdient daarom een herwaardering.
data.translatedTitle: In Asia, WWII was about a reckoning with European imperialism
data.translatedDescription: Historian Hans van de Ven writes in his new book that the West has underestimated the geopolitical developments that the Second World War set in motion in Asia. Its importance therefore deserves a reappraisal.

data.title: In de brieven van Du Perron aan zijn geliefde Bep is hij eerlijk op het pijnlijke af
data.description: Uit de fascinerende briefwisseling uit het interbellum tussen de invloedrijke schrijver E. du Perron en zijn vrouw Elisabeth de Roos komt een verlangen naar een ideale liefdesrelatie tussen man en vrouw naar voren.
data.translatedTitle: In Du Perron's letters to his beloved Bep he is honest to the point of being painful
data.translatedDescription: The fascinating exchange of letters from the interwar period between the influential writer E. du Perron and his wife Elisabeth de Roos reveals a desire for an ideal love relationship between man and woman.

data.title: 'Ik word gek, ik weet niet hoe ik uit deze gevangenis moet ontsnappen.' Deze bemanning zat vast in de Straat van Hormuz en overleefde een droneaanval
data.description: Nog altijd zitten duizenden bemanningsleden vast op schepen bij de Straat van Hormuz, die weer potdicht zit. De afgelopen maand werden twaalf schepen aangevallen, zeker zeventien bemanningsleden kwamen om. De Indiër Ramesh Dhandapani werd op een haar na geraakt.
data.translatedTitle: "I'm going crazy, I don't know how to escape this prison." This crew was trapped in the Strait of Hormuz and survived a drone attack
data.translatedDescription: Thousands of crew members are still stuck on ships near the Strait of Hormuz, which is closed again. Twelve ships were attacked last month and at least seventeen crew members were killed. Indian Ramesh Dhandapani was barely hit.

data.title: Een agnost die keihard werkte en bleef bidden. ‘Na het eten ging hij meteen weer aan het werk’
data.description: Hij was een onvermoeibare academicus. Dat zijn leven een filosofische afslag zou nemen, was niet meteen duidelijk.
data.translatedTitle: An agnostic who worked hard and kept praying. “After dinner he went straight back to work.”
data.translatedDescription: He was a tireless academic. It was not immediately clear that his life would take a philosophical turn.

data.description: Nach dem Showdown mit dem Müllritter sichert sich Nigel Farage in einem selbst für britische Verhältnisse ungewöhnlichen Vorgang erneut einen Sitz im Parlament. Eine brisante Altlast wird er dennoch nicht los.

data.translatedDescription: After the showdown with the Garbage Knight, Nigel Farage secured another seat in Parliament in a move that was unusual even by British standards. However, he cannot get rid of an explosive legacy.
