data.title: Tribunal Superior de Cuentas revela irregularidades en compra del avión presidencial
data.description: Tegucigalpa, Honduras.- El avión presidencial Embraer Legacy 600 ya se fue de Honduras, pero dejó tras de sí una estela de irregularidades, millones de lempiras bajo cuestionamiento y posibles delitos contra el patrimonio público. Un informe especial del Tribunal Superior de Cuentas (TSC) documentó una cadena de actuaciones irregulares y remitió el expediente al Ministerio Público para determinar si hubo responsabilidad penal. La investigación, identificada como Informe Especial P-02-2025/GVS-DAD-AFPSP, abarcó operaciones para su adquisición en la Tasa de Seguridad Poblacional. El primer cuestionamiento aparece en el origen mismo de la compra. El 21 de abril de 2014, el Consejo Nacional de Defensa y Seguridad autorizó mediante la Resolución CNDS-033/2014 el pago de un anticipo de un millón de dólares para reservar el avión . El desembolso se concretó el 12 de junio de ese año, por instrucciones de Juan Ramón Molina, coordinador del Comité Técnico del fideicomiso. El problema, según el TSC, es que en ese momento el artículo 84 de la Ley de Contratación del Estado prohibía adquirir maquinaria o equipo usado con fondos públicos. Fue hasta el 1 de octubre de 2014, mediante el Decreto Legislativo 35-2014, cuando se modificó la norma para permitir una excepción en determinadas adquisiciones aprobadas por el presidente en Consejo de Secretarios de Estado. Ocho días después se autorizó formalmente la compra. El TSC sostiene que “la secuencia de los hechos demuestra un incumplimiento claro a la normativa” y plantea interrogantes sobre si la reforma legal buscó justificar una actuación ya ejecutada. La factura proforma ECC-371/2014, emitida por ECC Leasing Company a través de Paulo Estevao de Carvalho, describió el Embraer Legacy 600, con capacidad para 13 pasajeros, dos motores AE3007A1E y un precio de 14 millones de dólares. Como ya se había entregado el millón de dólares, el saldo quedó en 13 millones. Pero el origen del dinero abrió otro frente. El convenio de cooperación entre Honduras y Taiwán contemplaba recursos para adquirir una aeronave militar, una flota de helicópteros y 40 ambulancias. Sin embargo, esos recursos terminaron vinculados con la compra del avión presidencial. El TSC concluyó que los fondos no fueron utilizados para cumplir con el propósito original del convenio y advirtió sobre una posible irregularidad en el manejo de recursos de cooperación internacional. La operación también involucró recursos del Fideicomiso para la Administración del Fondo de Protección y Seguridad Poblacional, cuyos fondos tenían como destino legal acciones de prevención y control de la delincuencia común y organizada. Aunque posteriormente los recursos fueron reintegrados mediante desembolsos de Taiwán, el TSC considera que “el uso inicial de esos fondos para financiar la compra del avión presidencial contradijo el destino establecido por la legislación”. Las anomalías continuaron durante la operación de la aeronave. El TSC encontró dos facturas de CAMP Systems International con el mismo número, IN123847, pero por montos diferentes. Una, emitida en septiembre de 2015, era por 13,150 dólares; la segunda, de octubre de 2016, ascendía a 26,950 dólares. Aunque las Fuerzas Armadas solicitaron únicamente el pago de la segunda, el Comité Técnico tramitó ambas, provocando un desembolso de 40,100 dólares, equivalente a L935,664.51. Para el TSC, la falta de verificación de los documentos “puede constituir un delito de malversación de fondos o fraude contra la administración pública”. Otro hallazgo golpea directamente los registros patrimoniales del Estado: es que el 31 de diciembre de 2014 se registraron L333,998,985.12 relacionados con la adquisición del avión Legacy y helicópteros Bell, pero la operación fue contabilizada como gasto y no como activo estatal. La Dirección Nacional de Bienes del Estado informó en 2024 que no tenía registro de la adquisición del Legacy 600, mientras que la Fuerza Aérea Hondureña sí lo había incorporado a sus inventarios con la matrícula FAH-001. El entonces comandante general de la FAH, Jorge Alberto Fernández López, dejó constancia del registro de la aeronave en los inventarios militares. Posteriormente, el subsecretario de Defensa, Orlando Garner Ordóñez, confirmó sus características: Embraer Legacy 600, serie 14501041, matrícula FAH-001 y dos motores AE3007A1E. Para el TSC, que la aeronave apareciera en los inventarios de la Fuerza Aérea, pero no como activo en los registros patrimoniales correspondientes, evidencia una posible inconsistencia en el tratamiento contable de un bien público de alto valor. El mantenimiento del avión presidencial también implicó millonarios gastos de viaje para personal de la Fuerza Aérea Hondureña (FAH). Entre 2016 y 2019, se asignaron viáticos a militares que, según la institución, participaron en misiones relacionadas con el mantenimiento del Legacy 600, así como en entrenamientos en el extranjero y vuelos solicitados por Casa Presidencial. En sus conclusiones, el TSC señala L11,085,602.14 en gastos de viaje. Sin embargo, el cuadro de asignaciones incluido en el propio informe suma L11,507,347.39. Entre quienes aparecen con los montos más altos están Marco Tulio Gonzáles Aguilar, con L2,519,736.13; Elvin Midel Oyuela Álvarez, con L1,926,424.61; Gerson Ali Rodríguez Pineda, con L1,923,365.33; Franklin Nectaly Galo Zúniga, con L1,911,062.77; y Noé Donay Hernández Hernández, con L1,837,468.89. El TSC también contrastó esas asignaciones con los registros del Banco Central de Honduras (BCH) y encontró transferencias por L9,075,440.25 a personal de la FAH durante el período revisado. La diferencia entre los montos asignados y los transferidos forma parte de la documentación analizada por los auditores. El principal cuestionamiento, sin embargo, está en el respaldo de esos desembolsos. Cuando el TSC pidió comprobar cómo se utilizaron los viáticos, la FAH informó que no encontró facturas de hotel, transporte u otros documentos que respaldaran las liquidaciones. La institución explicó que el procedimiento consistía en presentar copias del pasaporte y, cuando correspondía, los boletos aéreos, pero tampoco proporcionó una normativa específica que explicara cómo el Comité Técnico determinaba los montos entregados. Para el TSC, esa falta de documentación impidió comprobar adecuadamente el destino de los recursos y limitó la trazabilidad y transparencia del dinero público. El último hallazgo involucra a Pegasus S.A. En octubre de 2014, el Consejo Nacional de Defensa y Seguridad autorizó fondos para poner nuevamente en servicio los helicópteros FAH-947 y FAH-948. La resolución tenía una vigencia de seis meses y perdió validez el 11 de abril de 2015. Pese a ello, en diciembre de 2016 se emitieron facturas a favor de Pegasus por L4,767,860, y el dinero fue transferido en enero de 2017 mediante dos pagos: uno de L2,285,700 y otro de L2,482,160. Los auditores también encontraron diferencias en la documentación de esos pagos. Mientras los registros contables los describían como “servicio de transporte aéreo”, las facturas indicaban que se trataba de arrendamiento. Además, el TSC no encontró documentación suficiente que demostrara qué servicio prestó efectivamente Pegasus. A esto se sumó un cobro de L323,760 por Impuesto Sobre Ventas (ISV) en una de las facturas, pese a que los bienes y servicios adquiridos con recursos del Fondo de Protección y Seguridad Poblacional estaban exonerados de ese impuesto.
data.translatedTitle: Superior Court of Accounts reveals irregularities in the purchase of the presidential plane
data.translatedDescription: Tegucigalpa, Honduras.- The Embraer Legacy 600 presidential plane has already left Honduras, but it left behind a trail of irregularities, millions of lempiras under question and possible crimes against public assets. A special report from the Superior Court of Accounts (TSC) documented a chain of irregular actions and sent the file to the Public Ministry to determine if there was criminal responsibility. The investigation, identified as Special Report P-02-2025/GVS-DAD-AFPSP, covered operations for its acquisition in the Population Security Rate. The first question appears in the very origin of the purchase. On April 21, 2014, the National Defense and Security Council authorized through Resolution CNDS-033/2014 the payment of an advance payment of one million dollars to reserve the plane. The disbursement took place on June 12 of that year, on instructions from Juan Ramón Molina, coordinator of the trust's Technical Committee. The problem, according to the TSC, is that at that time article 84 of the State Procurement Law prohibited the acquisition of used machinery or equipment with public funds. It was not until October 1, 2014, through Legislative Decree 35-2014, when the rule was modified to allow an exception in certain acquisitions approved by the president in the Council of Secretaries of State. Eight days later the purchase was formally authorized. The TSC maintains that “the sequence of events demonstrates a clear non-compliance with the regulations” and raises questions about whether the legal reform sought to justify an action already carried out. Pro forma invoice ECC-371/2014, issued by ECC Leasing Company through Paulo Estevao de Carvalho, described the Embraer Legacy 600, with capacity for 13 passengers, two AE3007A1E engines and a price of 14 million dollars. Since the million dollars had already been delivered, the balance remained at 13 million. But the origin of money opened another front. The cooperation agreement between Honduras and Taiwan included resources to acquire a military aircraft, a fleet of helicopters and 40 ambulances. However, those resources ended up linked to the purchase of the presidential plane. The TSC concluded that the funds were not used to fulfill the original purpose of the agreement and warned about a possible irregularity in the management of international cooperation resources. The operation also involved resources from the Trust for the Administration of the Population Protection and Security Fund, whose funds were legally destined for actions to prevent and control common and organized crime. Although the resources were later repaid through disbursements from Taiwan, the TSC considers that “the initial use of these funds to finance the purchase of the presidential plane contradicted the destination established by the legislation.” The anomalies continued during the operation of the aircraft. The TSC found two invoices from CAMP Systems International with the same number, IN123847, but for different amounts. One, issued in September 2015, was for $13,150; the second, from October 2016, amounted to $26,950. Although the Armed Forces only requested payment for the second, the Technical Committee processed both, causing a disbursement of $40,100, equivalent to L935,664.51. For the TSC, the lack of verification of documents “may constitute a crime of embezzlement of funds or fraud against the public administration.” Another finding directly hits the State's property records: on December 31, 2014, L333,998,985.12 were recorded related to the acquisition of the Legacy airplane and Bell helicopters, but the operation was recorded as an expense and not as a state asset. The National Directorate of State Assets reported in 2024 that it had no record of the acquisition of the Legacy 600, while the Honduran Air Force had incorporated it into its inventories with the registration number FAH-001. The then general commander of the FAH, Jorge Alberto Fernández López, recorded the registration of the aircraft in the military inventories. Subsequently, the Undersecretary of Defense, Orlando Garner Ordóñez, confirmed its characteristics: Embraer Legacy 600, series 14501041, registration FAH-001 and two AE3007A1E engines. For the TSC, the fact that the aircraft appeared in the Air Force inventories, but not as an asset in the corresponding asset records, shows a possible inconsistency in the accounting treatment of a high-value public asset. The maintenance of the presidential plane also involved million-dollar travel expenses for personnel of the Honduran Air Force (FAH). Between 2016 and 2019, travel expenses were assigned to soldiers who, according to the institution, participated in missions related to the maintenance of the Legacy 600, as well as in training abroad and flights requested by the Presidential House. In its conclusions, the TSC indicates L11,085,602.14 in travel expenses. However, the allocation table included in the report itself totals L11,507,347.39. Among those who appear with the highest amounts are Marco Tulio Gonzáles Aguilar, with L2,519,736.13; Elvin Midel Oyuela Álvarez, with L1,926,424.61; Gerson Ali Rodríguez Pineda, with L1,923,365.33; Franklin Nectaly Galo Zúniga, with L1,911,062.77; and Noé Donay Hernández Hernández, with L1,837,468.89. The TSC also compared these allocations with the records of the Central Bank of Honduras (BCH) and found transfers of L9,075,440.25 to FAH personnel during the period reviewed. The difference between the amounts assigned and those transferred is part of the documentation analyzed by the auditors. The main question, however, is the support for these disbursements. When the TSC asked to verify how the travel expenses were used, the FAH reported that it found no hotel, transportation invoices or other documents that supported the settlements. The institution explained that the procedure consisted of presenting copies of the passport and, when applicable, the airline tickets, but it did not provide specific regulations that explained how the Technical Committee determined the amounts delivered. For the TSC, this lack of documentation prevented adequate verification of the destination of the resources and limited the traceability and transparency of public money. The latest discovery involves Pegasus S.A. In October 2014, the National Defense and Security Council authorized funds to return the FAH-947 and FAH-948 helicopters to service. The resolution was valid for six months and lost validity on April 11, 2015. Despite this, in December 2016 invoices were issued in favor of Pegasus for L4,767,860, and the money was transferred in January 2017 through two payments: one of L2,285,700 and another of L2,482,160. Auditors also found differences in the documentation of those payments. While the accounting records described them as “air transportation service,” the invoices indicated that it was leasing. Furthermore, the TSC did not find sufficient documentation to demonstrate what service Pegasus actually provided. Added to this was a charge of L323,760 for Sales Tax (ISV) on one of the invoices, despite the fact that the goods and services acquired with resources from the Population Protection and Security Fund were exempt from that tax.

data.title: Corredor seco pierde el 100 % de la cosecha de subsistencia
data.description: Tegicigalpa, Honduras.- El 100 % de la cosecha destinada al consumo familiar se perdió en el corredor seco debido a las condiciones climáticas adversas, informó el ministro de la Secretaría de Agricultura y Ganadería (SAG), Moisés Molina. Molina explicó que las pérdidas corresponden principalmente a cultivos de subsistencia, producidos por familias para su propio consumo y no para la comercialización. Sin embargo, reconoció que la situación representa un fuerte golpe para los hogares que dependen de esas cosechas para alimentarse y generar parte de sus ingresos. “No tenemos ningún peligro de hambruna ni problemas alimenticios en el país, el problema está resuelto”, aseguró el funcionario. Señaló que la pérdida de los cultivos familiares no compromete, por ahora, el abastecimiento nacional de granos, aunque admitió que también existen zonas donde la producción comercial resultó afectada. En el Corredor Seco viven más de 2.2 millones de hondureños. Molina indicó que el Gobierno debe priorizar la asistencia humanitaria para las familias que perdieron sus cultivos, debido a que en muchos casos la cosecha representa su principal medio de subsistencia. Ante los pronósticos climáticos desfavorables, el funcionario advirtió que no sería conveniente entregar semillas y fertilizantes para una nueva siembra, debido al riesgo de que los productores vuelvan a perder sus cultivos.
data.translatedTitle: Dry corridor loses 100% of subsistence harvest
data.translatedDescription: Tegicigalpa, Honduras.- 100% of the harvest intended for family consumption was lost in the dry corridor due to adverse weather conditions, reported the minister of the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock (SAG), Moisés Molina. Molina explained that the losses correspond mainly to subsistence crops, produced by families for their own consumption and not for commercialization. However, he acknowledged that the situation represents a strong blow for households that depend on these crops to feed themselves and generate part of their income. “We do not have any danger of famine or food problems in the country, the problem is solved,” said the official. He pointed out that the loss of family crops does not compromise, for now, the national supply of grains, although he admitted that there are also areas where commercial production was affected. More than 2.2 million Hondurans live in the Dry Corridor. Molina indicated that the Government must prioritize humanitarian assistance for families that lost their crops, because in many cases the harvest represents their main means of subsistence. Given the unfavorable weather forecasts, the official warned that it would not be advisable to deliver seeds and fertilizers for a new sowing, due to the risk that producers would lose their crops again.

data.title: Honduras regresa al Ciadi el 16 de agosto tras casi dos años fuera
data.description: Tegucigalpa, Honduras.- Honduras volverá este 16 de agosto al Centro Internacional de Arreglo de Diferencias Relativas a Inversiones (Ciadi), organismo dependiente del Grupo del Banco Mundial (BM), tras casi dos años de ausencia. Con esta decisión, el Gobierno de Nasry Asfura busca fortalecer la seguridad jurídica, recuperar la credibilidad internacional y enviar un mensaje de confianza a los inversionistas globales. El retorno al Ciadi permitirá a Honduras contar nuevamente con este mecanismo internacional para la resolución de controversias relacionadas con inversiones. La medida forma parte de los esfuerzos del Gobierno para mejorar las condiciones para la inversión y reforzar la confianza de empresas e inversionistas extranjeros en el país. El Gobierno de Xiomara Castro formalizó la salida del Ciadi el 25 de agosto de 2024, al argumentar que la medida buscaba proteger la soberanía nacional, salvaguardar las finanzas públicas y evitar demandas multimillonarias de inversionistas extranjeros. No obstante, la decisión no evitó que el Estado recibiera nuevas demandas ni que los procesos existentes continuaran su curso. La medida fue cuestionada por diversos sectores, que consideraron que enviaba un mensaje negativo a los inversionistas al poner en duda las garantías de seguridad jurídica. Honduras tenía 35 años de pertenecer a este centro internacional de resolución de controversias. El 6 de marzo de 2026, Nasry Asfura, presidente de la República, firmó el Convenio sobre Arreglo de Diferencias Relativas a Inversiones entre Estados y Nacionales de Otros Estados, también conocido como Convenio Ciadi, con el objetivo de fortalecer la inversión y enviar un mensaje de confianza a los inversionistas. Es importante destacar que la salida de Honduras del Ciadi no detuvo las demandas contra el Estado. Por ejemplo, después del anuncio de la salida y antes de que esta se oficializara, el 8 de agosto de 2024 se sumaron dos demandas más del sector de energía renovable. Posteriormente, tras la salida oficial de Honduras del Ciadi, se sumó una nueva demanda, registrada el 15 de mayo de 2025, relacionada con proyectos inmobiliarios y de desarrollo vinculados al sector de la construcción. Actualmente, están pendientes 14 casos relacionados con los sectores de energía, transporte, construcción, finanzas, servicios financieros y otras industrias. En entrevistas anteriores, Roberto Lagos, presidente del Banco Central de Honduras (BCH), se refirió a la reincorporación al Ciadi como una victoria temprana dentro de una administración enfocada en atraer inversión extranjera directa. “El Ciadi sirve para tener reglas claras”. Lagos también indicó que en tres años ingresaron nuevas demandas que ponen en riesgo las finanzas públicas del país. A su vez, Emilio Hernández Hércules, ministro de Finanzas, sostuvo que solo países como Cuba y Venezuela están fuera del Ciadi. “Este sistema de conciliación lo que provee a la Procuraduría General de la Republica un espacio donde podamos reparar aquellas demandas internacionales que están afectando los recursos económicos de nuestro país”. Hércules agregó que ha habido empresas que con el anuncio del retorno de Honduras al Ciadi, se han acercado para conciliar las demandas con el Estado de manera favorable y sin que esto impacte las finanzas públicas. En julio de 2026, la Procuraduría General de la República (PGR) informó que auditaría demandas recientes contra el Estado de Honduras tras el retorno del país al Ciadi. "Estamos trabajando en una auditoría, que posteriormente se dará a conocer, y revisará cada uno de los casos no solo de bufetes nacionales, sino también de bufetes internacionales, porque estamos tratando de identificar bufetes nacionales que han actuado para desfavorecer al Estado de Honduras; ya no podemos seguir ordeñando al Estado de Honduras de una manera grosera, es injusto", declaró en su momento José Francisco Quiroz, subprocurador de la República. Javier Briceño, experto en arbitraje internacional, declaró que el retorno de Honduras al Ciadi convierte al país en un territorio más atractivo para los inversionistas extranjeros, ya que su salida lo colocaba en desventaja frente a otros países de la región que sí pertenecen al organismo arbitral internacional, como El Salvador, Guatemala, Costa Rica y Panamá. Briceño explicó que tanto el Estado como los inversionistas buscan un organismo independiente e imparcial que actúe como árbitro y en el que ambas partes consideren que pueden obtener un resultado justo. “El arbitraje si bien es cierto una figura más rápida y eficiente que un proceso judicial, por la complejidad de la materia no se resuelve en un día o dos, en promedio un caso Ciadi puede tomar tres años, el proceso más corto que se llevó duró un año y el más largo que sigue activo lleva 10 años”. A modo de ejemplo, refirió que en el caso de Honduras Próspera Inc., registrado en 2023, se prevé que la sentencia arbitral salga para 2028. “Cada caso tiene su calendario procesal”, acotó. Honduras Próspera Inc. demandó al Estado de Honduras ante el Ciadi por más de $10,700 millones tras la derogación de la ley de las Zede (Zonas Especiales de Desarrollo y Empleo). La empresa redujo posteriormente su reclamo económico a unos $1,630 millones. (, en un proceso que pone en tensión la soberanía nacional y el riesgo regulatorio.) Agregó que lo mejor es la conciliación y la negociación, pero que esto depende de la voluntad de ambas partes. “Una negociación parte de poder ceder a ciertas posturas”. Briceño indicó que lo mejor es la conciliación y, a modo de ejemplo, señaló que en el caso de Honduras Próspera Inc. la principal petición es que se le permita seguir operando y se le reconozcan los derechos que la normativa le otorga. “Es mucho más sencillo llegar a un punto medio cuando las partes tienen esta apertura y debe aprovecharse, debe aprovecharse porque es un caso complejo y tiene varias aristas, pero, también implica una responsabilidad para el Estado bastante considerable, en caso de que el caso salga a favor del inversionista”, explicó el experto.
data.translatedTitle: Honduras returns to ICSID on August 16 after almost two years away
data.translatedDescription: Tegucigalpa, Honduras.- Honduras will return this August 16 to the International Center for Settlement of Investment Disputes (ICSID), an organization dependent on the World Bank Group (WB), after almost two years of absence. With this decision, the Government of Nasry Asfura seeks to strengthen legal security, recover international credibility and send a message of confidence to global investors. The return to ICSID will allow Honduras to once again have this international mechanism for the resolution of disputes related to investments. The measure is part of the Government's efforts to improve conditions for investment and reinforce the confidence of foreign companies and investors in the country. The Government of Xiomara Castro formalized the departure from ICSID on August 25, 2024, arguing that the measure sought to protect national sovereignty, safeguard public finances and avoid multimillion-dollar lawsuits from foreign investors. However, the decision did not prevent the State from receiving new demands nor from existing processes continuing their course. The measure was questioned by various sectors, which considered that it sent a negative message to investors by calling into question the guarantees of legal security. Honduras had been part of this international dispute resolution center for 35 years. On March 6, 2026, Nasry Asfura, President of the Republic, signed the Convention on the Settlement of Investment Disputes between States and Nationals of Other States, also known as the ICSID Convention, with the aim of strengthening investment and sending a message of confidence to investors. It is important to highlight that the departure of Honduras from ICSID did not stop lawsuits against the State. For example, after the announcement of the exit and before it became official, on August 8, 2024, two more demands from the renewable energy sector were added. Subsequently, after the official departure of Honduras from ICSID, a new lawsuit was added, registered on May 15, 2025, related to real estate and development projects linked to the construction sector. Currently, 14 cases related to the energy, transportation, construction, finance, financial services and other industries are pending. In previous interviews, Roberto Lagos, president of the Central Bank of Honduras (BCH), referred to the reincorporation of the ICSID as an early victory within an administration focused on attracting foreign direct investment. “ICSID serves to have clear rules.” Lagos also indicated that in three years new demands were filed that put the country's public finances at risk. In turn, Emilio Hernández Hércules, Minister of Finance, maintained that only countries like Cuba and Venezuela are outside the ICSID. "This conciliation system provides the Attorney General's Office with a space where we can repair those international demands that are affecting the economic resources of our country." Hércules added that there have been companies that, with the announcement of the return of Honduras to ICSID, have approached to reconcile the demands with the State in a favorable manner and without this impacting public finances. In July 2026, the Attorney General's Office (PGR) reported that it would audit recent lawsuits against the State of Honduras after the country's return to ICSID. "We are working on an audit, which will later be announced, and will review each of the cases not only of national law firms, but also of international law firms, because we are trying to identify national law firms that have acted to disadvantage the State of Honduras; we can no longer continue milking the State of Honduras in a rude manner, it is unfair," declared José Francisco Quiroz, Deputy Attorney General of the Republic at the time. Javier Briceño, an expert in international arbitration, declared that the return of Honduras to the ICSID makes the country a more attractive territory for foreign investors, since its departure placed it at a disadvantage compared to other countries in the region that do belong to the international arbitration body, such as El Salvador, Guatemala, Costa Rica and Panama. Briceño explained that both the State and investors are looking for an independent and impartial body to act as an arbitrator and in which both parties consider that they can obtain a fair result. "Although arbitration is certainly a faster and more efficient procedure than a judicial process, due to the complexity of the matter it is not resolved in a day or two, on average an ICSID case can take three years, the shortest process that took place lasted one year and the longest that is still active takes 10 years." As an example, he said that in the case of Honduras Próspera Inc., registered in 2023, the arbitration ruling is expected to be issued in 2028. “Each case has its procedural calendar,” he said. Honduras Próspera Inc. sued the State of Honduras before the ICSID for more than $10.7 billion after the repeal of the Zede (Special Development and Employment Zones) law. The company later reduced its financial claim to about $1.63 billion. (, in a process that puts national sovereignty and regulatory risk in tension.) He added that the best thing is conciliation and negotiation, but that this depends on the will of both parties. “A negotiation starts from being able to give in to certain positions.” Briceño indicated that the best thing is conciliation and, as an example, he pointed out that in the case of Honduras Próspera Inc. the main request is that it be allowed to continue operating and that the rights that the regulations grant it be recognized. “It is much easier to reach a middle point when the parties have this openness and it must be taken advantage of, it must be taken advantage of because it is a complex case and has several aspects, but it also implies a quite considerable responsibility for the State, in case the case turns out in favor of the investor,” explained the expert.

data.title: Presidente Asfura pide aprobar reformas para frenar las pérdidas de la ENEE
data.description: Tegucigalpa, Honduras.- El presidente de Honduras, Nasry ‘Tito’ Asfura , pidió este miércoles al Congreso Nacional aprobar las reformas energéticas para "administrar mejor" la estatal eléctrica del país y frenar sus pérdidas millonarias, un proyecto que la Unión Europea (UE) está dispuesta a respaldar con una subvención de 9,2 millones de dólares. El Ejecutivo de Asfura presentó ante el Parlamento a inicios de junio pasado las reformas a la Ley del Subsector Eléctrico con el objetivo de sanear la Empresa Nacional de Energía Eléctrica (ENEE), que registra pérdidas que rozan los 600 millones de dólares anuales, según cifras oficiales. "Apruébenmela, yo les voy a dar respuestas. Esa ley no favorece a nadie, favorece a Honduras", subrayó Asfura a periodistas tras participar en un evento con motivo del Día Nacional de la Libre Competencia, dado que el Parlamento aún no ha comenzado a discutir la iniciativa. El mandatario señaló que no se opone a que el proyecto de reformas energéticas incorpore una disposición que garantice que la empresa eléctrica continúe siendo propiedad del Estado hondureño, ante los cuestionamientos de sectores de la oposición que sostienen que la iniciativa busca privatizar la ENEE. "Acá la ENEE es de Honduras, pero no puede seguir quebrada, tenemos que enderezarla, porque eso golpea al país (...) o nos ponemos en orden los que consumimos energía, pagamos lo que debemos pagar, o no vamos a salir adelante", enfatizó. El gobernante afirmó que las reformas a la Ley del Subsector Eléctrico son necesarias para "ordenar" la estatal elétrica, cuya situación financiera considera un obstáculo para la competitividad del país. "¿Cómo vamos a competir con una ENEE que todos los días pierde 50 millones de lempiras (unos 1,9 millones de dólares)? No podemos seguir así", enfatizó Asfura, quien dijo comprender las diferencias políticas en el Parlamento, pero pidió a los diputados anteponer el interés nacional a cualquier consideración partidista. La jefa de Cooperación de la UE en Tegucigalpa, Cristina Marín, dijo a EFE que, de aprobarse las reformas, el bloque prevé aportar a Honduras 8 millones de euros (unos 9,2 millones de dólares) en fondos no reembolsables para apalancar inversiones de hasta 500 millones de euros (unos 577,1 millones de dólares) del Banco Europeo de Inversiones (BEI). La UE analiza, además, un potencial financiamiento inicial de 200 millones de euros (unos 230,8 millones de dólares), señaló la diplomática, quien consideró necesaria la aprobación de las reformas energéticas para crear las condiciones que permitan concretar nuevas inversiones en el sector.
data.translatedTitle: President Asfura asks to approve reforms to stop ENEE's losses
data.translatedDescription: Tegucigalpa, Honduras.- The president of Honduras, Nasry 'Tito' Asfura, asked this Wednesday the National Congress to approve energy reforms to "better manage" the country's state electricity company and stop its million-dollar losses, a project that the European Union (EU) is willing to support with a subsidy of 9.2 million dollars. The Asfura Executive presented to Parliament at the beginning of last June the reforms to the Electricity Subsector Law with the objective of cleaning up the National Electric Energy Company (ENEE), which registers losses approaching 600 million dollars annually, according to official figures. "Approve it, I will give you answers. This law does not favor anyone, it favors Honduras," Asfura stressed to journalists after participating in an event on the occasion of National Free Competition Day, given that Parliament has not yet begun to discuss the initiative. The president indicated that he is not opposed to the energy reform project incorporating a provision that guarantees that the electric company continues to be property of the Honduran State, in the face of questions from sectors of the opposition who maintain that the initiative seeks to privatize ENEE. "Here the ENEE is from Honduras, but it cannot continue to be broken, we have to straighten it out, because that hits the country (...) or those of us who consume energy get our act together, we pay what we have to pay, or we are not going to get ahead," he emphasized. The president affirmed that the reforms to the Electricity Subsector Law are necessary to "organize" the state electricity company, whose financial situation he considers an obstacle to the country's competitiveness. "How are we going to compete with an ENEE that loses 50 million lempiras (about 1.9 million dollars) every day? We cannot continue like this," emphasized Asfura, who said he understood the political differences in Parliament, but asked the deputies to put the national interest before any partisan considerations. The head of EU Cooperation in Tegucigalpa, Cristina Marín, told EFE that, if the reforms are approved, the bloc plans to provide Honduras with 8 million euros (about 9.2 million dollars) in non-refundable funds to leverage investments of up to 500 million euros (about 577.1 million dollars) from the European Investment Bank (EIB). The EU is also analyzing a potential initial financing of 200 million euros (about 230.8 million dollars), said the diplomat, who considered the approval of the energy reforms necessary to create the conditions that allow new investments to be made in the sector.

data.title: Construcción de rotonda en El Lolo apenas alcanza un 15% de avance
data.description: Tegucigalpa, Honduras. - ​​​​​​La construcción de la rotonda en el desvío hacia El Lolo apenas registra un 15% de avance y se prevé que facilite la circulación de vehículos entre la zona norte y el centro de Tegucigalpa y Comayagüela. Actualmente, los trabajos incluyen la construcción de un muro perimetral y obras de tuberías . La intervención comenzó hace aproximadamente 28 días y forma parte de un proyecto que contempla varias obras complementarias para ordenar el tránsito en este sector de la capital. “La rotonda en la que se está construyendo un muro perimetral y lleva obras de tuberías está proyectada para facilitar el paso de los vehículos que llegan desde la zona norte con dirección al centro de la capital y viceversa”, afirmó el especialista. La obra también está vinculada con el reordenamiento vial de los vehículos que llegan desde San Pedro Sula, particularmente en el sector de El Durazno y su conexión con El Lolo. Como parte del proyecto, s e contempla la construcción de una vía de doble carril, espacios de estacionamiento, una bahía, áreas verdes, barandales y la habilitación de la calle en el punto donde se desarrolla la rotonda. “Para ejecutar los trabajos se cuenta con 70 y 80 trabajadores diarios donde se labora hasta las 8:00 de la noche, con el propósito de avanzar sin generar mayores afectaciones al tránsito durante el día”, expresó. Asimismo, los trabajos incluyen infraestructura de captación y tuberías para atender problemas relacionados con la falta de agua en algunos puntos del sector. El personal a cargo de la obra pidió paciencia a la población debido a los retrasos registrados durante la ejecución del proyecto. Tanto el ingeniero como el arquitecto expresaron: “Pedimos a la población que tenga calma, ya que este proyecto ha tenido muchos retrasos debido a obras complementarias que se han presentado durante la intervención”. El ministro de la Secretaría de Infraestructura y Transporte, Aníbal Ehler, aseguró en julio pasado que el proyecto lleva un 90% de avance en sus dos primeras etapas y que están finalizando los 7.5 kilómetros que van del mall Premier hasta El Guanábano. La ampliación de la carretera hacia Olancho fue dividida en diferentes fases. La primera comprende el tramo que llega hasta el sector de El Guanábano y cuenta con pavimento de concreto hidráulico. La segunda corresponde al tramo entre el mall Premier y la colonia Campo Cielo, donde los trabajos principales ya fueron ejecutados. La tercera fase contempla el tramo entre el Mall Premier y Campo Cielo. Este sector cuenta con concreto asfáltico y está en proceso de gestión para su ejecución. La ampliación comprende aproximadamente 7.7 kilómetros y busca convertir la carretera de dos a cuatro carriles para mejorar la movilidad y la conexión con la zona oriental del país. La inversión inicial aumentó hasta los 205.6 millones de lempiras debido a la incorporación de trabajos adicionales en distintos puntos del proyecto. Una falla geológica en las inmediaciones de la gasolinera Texaco también ha retrasado los trabajos, ya que en ese punto se ejecutaron estudios y obras especiales para reducir riesgos y resguardar la infraestructura existente.
data.translatedTitle: Construction of a roundabout in El Lolo is barely 15% complete
data.translatedDescription: Tegucigalpa, Honduras. - ​​​​​​The construction of the roundabout on the detour to El Lolo is barely 15% complete and is expected to facilitate the circulation of vehicles between the northern area and the center of Tegucigalpa and Comayagüela. Currently, work includes the construction of a perimeter wall and pipe works. The intervention began approximately 28 days ago and is part of a project that includes several complementary works to organize traffic in this sector of the capital. “The roundabout in which a perimeter wall is being built and involves pipeline works is designed to facilitate the passage of vehicles arriving from the northern area towards the center of the capital and vice versa,” said the specialist. The work is also linked to the road reorganization of vehicles arriving from San Pedro Sula, particularly in the El Durazno sector and its connection with El Lolo. As part of the project, the construction of a double-lane road, parking spaces, a bay, green areas, railings and the preparation of the street at the point where the roundabout is developed is contemplated. "To carry out the work, there are 70 and 80 daily workers where they work until 8:00 at night, with the purpose of moving forward without generating major effects on traffic during the day," he said. Likewise, the works include collection infrastructure and pipes to address problems related to the lack of water in some parts of the sector. The personnel in charge of the work asked the population for patience due to the delays recorded during the execution of the project. Both the engineer and the architect expressed: “We ask the population to be calm, since this project has had many delays due to complementary works that have been presented during the intervention.” The Minister of the Secretariat of Infrastructure and Transportation, Aníbal Ehler, assured last July that the project is 90% complete in its first two stages and that the 7.5 kilometers that go from the Premier mall to El Guanábano are finishing. The expansion of the highway to Olancho was divided into different phases. The first includes the section that reaches the El Guanábano sector and has hydraulic concrete pavement. The second corresponds to the section between the Premier mall and the Campo Cielo neighborhood, where the main works have already been carried out. The third phase includes the section between Mall Premier and Campo Cielo. This sector has asphalt concrete and is in the management process for its execution. The expansion covers approximately 7.7 kilometers and seeks to convert the highway from two to four lanes to improve mobility and connection with the eastern part of the country. The initial investment increased to 205.6 million lempiras due to the incorporation of additional work at different points of the project. A geological fault in the vicinity of the Texaco gas station has also delayed the work, since special studies and works were carried out at that point to reduce risks and protect the existing infrastructure.

data.title: Junaci Borca su tinejdžeri Jurkas i Deket: "Pokazali smo karakter i prošli jer smo šampioni"
data.description: Borac je nakon velike drame i penala u Bjelorusiji prošao u play-off Konferencijske lige, a nakon pobjede protiv ML Vitebska oglasili su se junaci pobjede, tinejdžeri Mladen Jurkas (18) i Matej Deket (16).
data.translatedTitle: The heroes of Borac are teenagers Jurkas and Deket: "We showed character and passed because we are champions"
data.translatedDescription: After a big drama and a penalty in Belarus, Borac made it to the play-off of the Conference League, and after the victory against ML Vitebsk, the heroes of the victory, teenagers Mladen Jurkas (18) and Matej Deket (16), announced themselves.

data.title: Nicole Kidman o  razvodu od Keitha Urbana: Imala sam drugačiju viziju svog života, ali situacija je sada ovakva

data.translatedTitle: Nicole Kidman on the divorce from Keith Urban: I had a different vision of my life, but the situation is like this now
data.translatedDescription: In a new interview for the British edition of Vogue magazine, Australian-American actress Nicole Kidman talked, among other things, about how she thought her life after her divorce from Keith Urban would be different than it is.

data.title: Prizor kod Omiša sliči scenama iz horor filmova: Vatra "progutala" objekte, izgorjela auta ostavljena na cesti

data.translatedDescription: Omiš firefighters, with the help of colleagues from other cities, are trying to put out the fire that broke out last night in Lokva Rogoznica and spread towards Omiš.

data.translatedDescription: Nigel Farage has returned to the British Parliament after winning the election that was the subject of public ridicule, AP reported from London.

data.translatedTitle: The four Canadians who went to extinguish the fire near Omiš are among the most followed flights on FlightRadar
data.translatedDescription: The Croatian Canadians who fought the flare-up near Omiš were this morning among the most followed flights on the popular Flightradar24 platform.

data.title: Rumunija ugasila jedinu nuklearnu elektranu zbog niskog vodostaja Dunava
data.description: Rumunija je ugasila nuklearnu elektranu Cernavoda nakon što je dugotrajna vrućina spustila vodostaj Dunava, čija se voda koristi za hlađenje postrojenja.
data.translatedTitle: Romania shut down the only nuclear power plant due to the low water level of the Danube
data.translatedDescription: Romania shut down the Cernavoda nuclear power plant after prolonged heat lowered the water level of the Danube, whose water is used to cool the plant.

data.title: Koenigsegg hiperautomobilom CCGT1 odao počast GT1 projektu koji nikada nije zaživio
data.description: Koenigseggov originalni model CCGT napravljen je za GT1 seriju, potom je testiran, a onda ostavljen po strani kada su se pravila promijenila, tako da nikada nije učestvovao u takmičenju. Međutim, sada ima budućnost u historijskim utrkama i modernu cestovnu posvetu pod nazivom CCGT1.
data.translatedTitle: Koenigsegg paid tribute to the GT1 project that never came to life with the CCGT1 hypercar
data.translatedDescription: Koenigsegg's original CCGT model was built for the GT1 series, then tested and then shelved when the rules changed, so it never competed. However, it now has a future in historic racing and a modern road dedication called the CCGT1.

data.title: Ogroman požar došao do centra Omiša, strahoviti prizori: Ima povrijeđenih, evakuisani ljudi dok gradom odjekuju sirene
data.description: Veliki šumski požar koji je tokom protekle večeri izbio u Lokvi Rogoznici noćas se proširio prema Omišu i stigao nadomak samog gradskog središta.
data.translatedTitle: A huge fire reached the center of Omiš, terrifying scenes: There are injured people, evacuated people while sirens echo through the city
data.translatedDescription: The large forest fire that broke out in Lokva Rogoznica last night spread towards Omiš and reached the very center of the city.

data.title: Na suđenju otkriveno da je Lindsay Clancy pretraživala psihozu i načine smrti
data.description: Na suđenju Lindsay Clancy u Massachusettsu izneseni su podaci s njenog telefona koji pokazuju da je prije ubistva troje djece tražila informacije o halucinacijama, psihozi i samoubistvu.
data.translatedTitle: At the trial it was revealed that Lindsay Clancy had researched psychosis and ways of death
data.translatedDescription: At the trial of Lindsay Clancy in Massachusetts, data from her phone was presented showing that before murdering her three children she had sought information about hallucinations, psychosis and suicide.

data.title: Jared Kushner iduće sedmice putuje u Izrael i Egipat zbog pregovora o Gazi
data.description: Jared Kushner, zet predsjednika Donalda Trumpa i njegov pregovarač, iduće sedmice putuje u Izrael i Egipat kako bi pokušao pokrenuti plan za okončanje sukoba u Gazi.
data.translatedTitle: Jared Kushner is traveling to Israel and Egypt next week for talks on Gaza
data.translatedDescription: Jared Kushner, President Donald Trump's son-in-law and his negotiator, is traveling to Israel and Egypt next week to try to launch a plan to end the conflict in Gaza.

data.title: "Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition" stiže 1. oktobra i donosi novi dio priče
data.description: "Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition" bit će objavljen 1. oktobra za PlayStation 5. To je gotovo tačno godinu dana nakon što je izašla osnovna verzija igre. Complete Edition predstavlja pravo unapređenje s mnogo novog sadržaja.
data.translatedTitle: "Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition" arrives on October 1 and brings a new part of the story
data.translatedDescription: "Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition" will be released on October 1st for PlayStation 5. That's almost exactly one year after the base version of the game was released. The Complete Edition is a real upgrade with a lot of new content.

data.title: Analitičar o strategiji Teherana: Iran namjerno odugovlači rat, više se ne boje američke invazije
data.description: Iran ima za cilj produžiti trenutni sukob jer smatra da ekonomski pritisak ne predstavlja egzistencijalnu prijetnju opstanku tamošnje vlade, ocijenio je u razgovoru za Al Jazeeru Michael Stephens, viši saradnik Kraljevskog instituta ujedinjenih službi (RUSI).
data.translatedTitle: An analyst on Tehran's strategy: Iran is deliberately delaying the war, they are no longer afraid of an American invasion
data.translatedDescription: Iran aims to prolong the current conflict because it believes that economic pressure does not represent an existential threat to the survival of the government there, said Michael Stephens, senior fellow of the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI), in an interview with Al Jazeera.

data.title: Američka vojska u ratu s Iranom ostala bez četvrtina dronova, pojedinačno koštaju i do 50 miliona dolara
data.description: Američka vojska izgubila je najmanje 45 dronova MQ-9 Reaper tokom rata s Iranom, što je oko 25 posto flote. Letjelice su intenzivno korištene oko Hormuškog moreuza.
data.translatedTitle: The American army lost a quarter of its drones in the war with Iran, they cost up to 50 million dollars individually
data.translatedDescription: The US military lost at least 45 MQ-9 Reaper drones during the war with Iran, about 25 percent of the fleet. Aircraft were used intensively around the Strait of Hormuz.

data.title: Najveći električni avion na svijetu uspješno obavio prvi let
data.description: Kompanija Heart Aerospace je saopćila da je uspješno obavljen prvi let prototipa njenog potpuno električnog aviona, demonstratora X1.
data.translatedTitle: The largest electric plane in the world successfully completed its first flight
data.translatedDescription: Heart Aerospace has announced the successful first flight of its all-electric prototype aircraft, the X1 demonstrator.

data.title: Xiaomi predstavio HyperOS 4 s novim "staklenim" izgledom i prilagodbama korisničkog interfejsa
data.description: Xiaomijeva izdanja sistema HyperOS nisu vezana za izdanja Androida. Kompanija trenutno objavljuje ažuriranje na Android 17 kao HyperOS 3, a sada je predstavila HyperOS 4, koji će najvjerovatnije biti zasnovan na istim temeljima, ali ipak donosi značajno izmijenjen korisnički interfejs.
data.translatedTitle: Xiaomi introduced HyperOS 4 with a new "glass" look and user interface adjustments
data.translatedDescription: Xiaomi's HyperOS releases are not tied to Android releases. The company is currently releasing the update to Android 17 as HyperOS 3, and now it has unveiled HyperOS 4, which will most likely be based on the same foundations, but still brings a significantly changed user interface.

data.title: Kultni The Prodigy priredio elektronski spektakl u Sarajevu: Pogledajte kako je izgledalo
data.description: Grupa The Prodigy večeras je uz prepoznatljivu energiju na stadionu Grbavica publici priredila spektakl elektronske muzike, a brojna publika uvjerila se još jednom zašto ova grupa ima kultni status u svijetu ove vrste muzike.
data.translatedTitle: The iconic The Prodigy staged an electronic spectacle in Sarajevo: See how it looked
data.translatedDescription: Tonight, with recognizable energy, the group The Prodigy gave the audience a spectacle of electronic music at the Grbavica stadium, and a large audience was once again convinced why this group has a cult status in the world of this type of music.

data.title: Saša Matić otvorio Summertime Madness Festival u Sarajevu, večer nije mogla proći bez hita Halida Bešlića
data.description: Regionalna muzička zvijezda Saša Matić večeras je koncertom na Trgu Oslobođenja - Alija Izetbegović u Sarajevu otvorio ovogodišnje izdanje festivala Summertime Madness.
data.translatedTitle: Saša Matić opened the Summertime Madness Festival in Sarajevo, the evening could not pass without Halid Bešlić's hit
data.translatedDescription: Regional music star Saša Matić opened this year's edition of the Summertime Madness festival tonight with a concert at Trg Oslobođenja - Alija Izetbegović in Sarajevo.

data.title: Od "glupih pitanja" do napuštanja govornice: Kako je Karoline Leavitt vodila rat s novinarima
data.description: Tokom rada u Bijeloj kući, sekretarica za štampu u odlasku Karoline Leavitt stekla je reputaciju svojim oštrim odgovorima novinarima, što je svojevrsni odjek spornog odnosa predsjednika Donalda Trumpa s medijima.
data.translatedTitle: From "stupid questions" to leaving the podium: How Karoline Leavitt waged war with the press
data.translatedDescription: During her tenure at the White House, outgoing press secretary Caroline Leavitt gained a reputation for her sharp responses to reporters, an echo of President Donald Trump's contentious relationship with the media.

data.title: Teorije zavjere ponovo oživjele: Kako je HAARP neosnovano okrivljen za smrt 270 ljudi u Kolumbiji
data.description: Nakon zemljotresa jačine 7,4 stepena koji je u ponedjeljak pogodio zapad Kolumbije, društvenim mrežama ponovo su se proširile tvrdnje da je katastrofu izazvao istraživački program HAARP iz Aljaske.
data.translatedTitle: Conspiracy theories revived: How HAARP was wrongly blamed for the deaths of 270 people in Colombia
data.translatedDescription: After the 7.4-magnitude earthquake that hit western Colombia on Monday, claims that the disaster was caused by the HAARP research program from Alaska spread again on social networks.

data.title: Zbog haotičnog stanja na nosaču USS Lincoln, Amerikanci na Bliski istok šalju hitnu zamjenu
data.description: Sjedinjene Američke Države pripremaju slanje nosača aviona USS George Washington na Bliski istok, gdje bi trebao zamijeniti USS Abraham Lincoln nakon više od 250 dana službe.

data.translatedDescription: The United States is preparing to send the aircraft carrier USS George Washington to the Middle East, where it is supposed to replace the USS Abraham Lincoln after more than 250 days of service.

data.title: Amerikanci pakuju kofere nakon 23 godine: Da li će povlačenje zapaliti novo bure baruta u Iraku?

Ovaj potez zatvara jedno od najturbulentnijih poglavlja moderne historije Bliskog istoka.

Selle jätnud komeedi küljest pudenenud osakesed võivad olla liivaterast rusikasuuruste tükkideni ning atmosfääri jõudes löövad need taeva hetkeks särama. data.translatedTitle: SCIENCE MINUTES «CLEAR PICTURE» ⟩ What happens when we say that «stars are falling» and what is actually a shower of stars
data.translatedDescription: Every August, the sky appears to be filled with shooting stars, but the Earth is actually traveling through a giant cosmic debris trail at this time. The particles that fall from the comet that left it can range from grains of sand to fist-sized pieces, and when they reach the atmosphere, they brighten the sky for a moment. Marek Strandberg explains why it all looks like a shower of stars when viewed from Earth.

data.translatedTitle: The head of the Ülemiste center raises money with a challenge for Karel Tilga, a decathlete
data.translatedDescription: The Ülemiste Night Run starts tonight, where thousands of recreational runners can try to run faster than Guido Pärnitsa, the manager of the Ülemiste Center. For each participant who completes the five-kilometer distance faster than him, the Ülemiste Center donates 5 euros to the decathlete Karel Tilga, who achieved the best place among Estonians at the European Championships, through the Estonian Athletics Association (EKJL).

data.title: Tropid kõrva ja unerohi sisse: lärmakas raudteeremont viis Ropka kandis une
data.description: Ääsi tänav Ropka linnajaos ei ole üldse raudtee ääres, aga ometigi viis ööl vastu neljapäeva raudteelt kostnud juba poolteist tundi väldanud talumatu müra asja nii kaugele, et väikese lapse ema Joanna Hoffmann saatis elukaaslase uurima, mis toimub.
data.translatedTitle: Pops in the ear and sleeping pills: the noisy railway repair caused Ropka to fall asleep
data.translatedDescription: Ääs street in the Ropka district is not at all by the railway, but nevertheless, the unbearable noise from the railway for an hour and a half last night brought the matter to such an extent that Joanna Hoffmann, the mother of a small child, sent her partner to find out what was going on.

data.title: LÄBIMURRE ⟩ Pika koroona sümptomitele leiti ajust füüsiline ja mõõdetav põhjus
data.description: Aastaid on pika koroona patsiendid otsinud vastuseid oma seletamatutele sümptomitele, puutudes sageli kokku meditsiinisüsteemi skepsisega. Nüüd tegid teadlased olulise läbimurde, muutes ajuskaneeringutel nähtavaks reaalsed kahjustused, mis selgitavad motivatsioonipuudust, aeglustunud liigutusi ja mäluhäireid.
data.translatedTitle: BREAKTHROUGH ⟩ A physical and measurable cause was found in the brain for long corona symptoms
data.translatedDescription: For years, chronic corona patients have searched for answers to their unexplained symptoms, often encountering skepticism from the medical system. Now researchers have made a major breakthrough, making real-world damage visible on brain scans that explains lack of motivation, slowed movements and memory impairment.

data.title: PALM JA HEREM ⟩ Sõjalised õppetunnid Ukrainast, mida Eesti peab rakendama: massiline täppistuli ja manöövrite kriis
data.description: Kui eelnevates peatükkides käsitletud lahinguvälja funktsioonid – juhtimine, luure, kaitstus, õhukaitse ja lahinguteenindustoetus – loovad eeldused lahingu pidamiseks, siis tuli ja manööver on sõjapidamise sisu, kirjutavad kindralmajor reservis Veiko-Vello Palm ja kindral reservis Martin Herem.
data.translatedTitle: PALM AND HEREM ⟩ Military lessons from Ukraine that Estonia must apply: mass precision fire and maneuver crisis
data.translatedDescription: If the functions of the battlefield discussed in the previous chapters - command, intelligence, protection, air defense and combat service support - create the prerequisites for conducting a battle, then fire and maneuver are the essence of warfare, write Major-General Veiko-Vello Palm in the reserve and General in the reserve Martin Herem.

data.title: VIDEO ⟩ Sajandi alguses topeltmõrva eest karistatud Raivi Saks seisis uuesti kohtu ees

See tähendab, et edaspidi võivad WRC-etappidel ja näiteks F1-sarjas venelased starti tulla oma riigilipu all ning etapivõidu korral kõlab võistluspaigas Venemaa riigihümn.
data.translatedTitle: Russians will be allowed into the WRC and back into the F1 series, but one important restriction remains
data.translatedDescription: The International Automobile Federation (FIA) announced on Thursday that it will remove the restrictions imposed on Russian drivers and teams in the racing series under their auspices. This means that in the future, in the WRC stages and, for example, in the F1 series, Russians can start under their national flag, and in the event of a stage victory, the Russian national anthem will be played at the competition venue.

data.title: Romania hosts its first multi-sport paralympic competition next month
data.description: The first edition of the Parasport Romania Games , the only national multi-sport para competition, is scheduled to take place in early September. Unlike competitions previously organized separately for each sport, the event will host multiple competitions simultaneously. The event gathers ten para sports and is meant to establish “a common platform dedicated to competition, performance and the development of Romanian para sport,” the National Paralympic Committee, the organizer of the event, said, quoted by News.ro . Over five days, the event is expected to bring to Bucharest more than 500 participants from Romania and abroad, including more than 300 athletes, as well as coaches, team staff, officials and delegations, for competitions in ten para sports. The events will take place at several sports venues across the capital, in a format combining National Championships and Open competitions. The Para Sport Romania Games 2026 program will feature ten disciplines: para table tennis, para swimming, para-athletics, para powerlifting, 3x3 wheelchair basketball, para-archery, adapted judo, wheelchair tennis, para climbing and para canoe. The National Championships will be open exclusively to Romanian athletes, with the results counting towards the selection of national teams that will represent Romania at international competitions. The Open competitions will be open to athletes from other countries. The event will take place from September 1 to September 5, 2026, at eight venues in Bucharest: Iolanda Balaș Soter Stadium, the National Tennis Center, CS Olimpia Bucharest, the Basketball Arena (FRB), Lia Manoliu National Sports Center, Arcul de Triumf National Sports Center, Vertical Spirit and Alexandru Ioan Cuza Park (IOR). “Para sport must be integrated, not separated. I know from my own experience as an athlete how important it is to have a framework in which you can demonstrate your worth and have your achievements recognized. Romania has talented athletes and important results, and the next step is to provide them with the conditions and visibility they need to continue to develop. The Para Sport Games were born out of this need: to bring athletes closer to the public and give para sport the place and visibility it deserves in Romanian sport,” Eduard Novak, president of the National Paralympic Committee, said. The Games will be open to the public, with free admission to the opening ceremony and all sporting competitions, with no prior registration required. (Photo: Riopatuca | Dreamstime.com ) simona@romania-insider.com

data.title: MMB Showcase Festival brings European soul, jazz-fusion, noise rock artists to Bucharest
data.description: MMB Showcase Festival , the festival associated with the Mastering the Music Business (MMB) conference, returns to Bucharest in early September with three nights of concerts at Club Expirat. The festival brings to the stage rising bands and artists from countries such as Romania, the Republic of Moldova, Germany, Greece, Estonia, Serbia and Bulgaria, in a line-up that ranges from soul and jazz-fusion to noise rock and psychedelic garage, the organizers said. The bands will perform both in front of the professionals attending the Mastering the Music Business conference, namely managers, booking agents, label and festival people, and journalists, and in front of the general public. This year's line-up mixes artists with careers spanning more than two decades with emerging voices. Cluj-based Grimus, who have opened for Queen, Red Hot Chili Peppers and Placebo, share the bill with Greece's Theodore, singled out by NPR for a Tiny Desk session, and with Charlotte Colace, the French-Cuban soul artist based in Berlin, winner of the Listen to Berlin Artist Award 2025. From Estonia come The Boondocks, repeat winners at the Estonian Music Awards, while the Balkans bring the psychedelic garage of Serbia's Phony Job and the noise rock with analogue video projections of Bulgaria's SLICR. The Romanian scene is represented by Alexandra Căpitănescu, winner of The Voice of Romania and the country's representative at Eurovision 2026, and by imstillFranci, a semi-finalist in the same Romanian Eurovision selection. Joining them on stage will be the jazz-fusion of Marquis Collective, the fuzzed-out psychedelic rock of Armand Popa, the art-folk of Cristina Lupu, the nostalgic dream-pop of duo miau.wav and the folk-inflected R&B of Simona Delegeanu. The international line-up is rounded out by the electronic energy of Moldova's Cosmos în Buzunar. MMB Showcase Festival takes place from September 1 to September 3. Entry to the event is free, on a first-come, first-served basis. (Illustration: the organizers) simona@romania-insider.com

data.title: CEC Bank, Exim Banca Romanească grant EUR 55 million financing for new Bucharest district heating plant CET Titan
data.description: CEC Bank and Exim Banca Românească have signed a RON 289 million (EUR 55.15 million) financing agreement for the development of the combined heat and power (CHP) plant CET Titan. The new CET Titan plant will be the first district heating power plant built from scratch in Bucharest since 1979. It is meant to “help strengthen the capital’s energy security, increase energy efficiency and reduce its environmental impact through the use of modern cogeneration technologies.” The investment is being carried out by Titan Power S.A., a project company majority-owned by SAPE S.A. and minority-owned by Electrocentrale Grup S.A., companies under the coordination of the Ministry of Energy. Electrocentrale Grup S.A. is currently undergoing a merger by absorption with SAPE S.A. The plant is expected to generate approximately 400 GWh of electricity annually, to be supplied to the National Energy System, as well as around 200 GWh of heat per year for Bucharest’s centralized district heating system. The plant will use modern natural gas-fired cogeneration technologies, reducing specific fuel consumption and greenhouse gas emissions, according to a description of the project. At the same time, it is designed to allow for the future use of lower-carbon fuels, including natural gas-hydrogen blends. Law firm NNDKP provided legal assistance in structuring and implementing the transaction. (Photo: Ginasanders | Dreamstime.com ) simona@romania-insider.com

data.title: Drone fragments removed from Romania’s touristic Costinești beach
data.description: Drone remains were discovered in the sea, close to Romania’s Costinești beach, on the Black Sea shore, on Thursday, August 13. The device was first noticed by employees in the area earlier in the morning. Initially, whether or not the device was a drone was not clear. Lifeguards then notified the authorities at around 8:15 AM and moved tourists away from the beach. Called to respond, military personnel also arrived on the beach in Costinești and confirmed that the object was a piece of an aerial drone, deciding to further restrict access to the beach. Military divers eventually recovered the piece of drone for examination. The authorities later informed that the drone fragment was not carrying explosives. Present at a public event, Romania’s interim defense minister Radu Miruță said that “drone alerts are happening constantly, unfortunately, as a result of the Russian Federation’s aggression in Ukraine,” according to Digi24 . “The surface area of the Black Sea is double the area of Romania. In a sector of the Black Sea, a literal war is taking place. There are situations such as the one this morning in which the waves bring drone remains resulting from this war also to the shore of the Black Sea, depending on the current. It is our duty, which the Romanian Army is fulfilling, to contribute with everything we can so that this war remains as far as possible from the national territory,” the minister argued. Earlier this week, two Gerbera-type drones were destroyed by divers of the Romanian Army in the exclusive economic zone, approximately 90 nautical miles (around 165 kilometers) from Constanța, in the Neptun Deep exploitation area . In a meeting on Wednesday, August 12, ambassadors of NATO member countries condemned Russia for drone incursions on the territories of Romania and Poland. radu@romania-insider.com (Photo source: Trentinness|Dreamstime.com )

data.title: Romanian carrier TAROM unveils first Boeing 737 MAX 8
data.description: TAROM, Romania’s ailing national carrier, has presented the first Boeing 737 MAX 8 that will enter its fleet. The company released a video of the plane on Tuesday, August 11, showing the stages through which the new aircraft is passing before it will be put into operation. The aircraft, currently at the Boeing factory in Renton, Washington, has already carried out its first test flight, has been painted in TAROM colors, and is to be delivered to the Romanian air operator. The new Boeing 737-8 has a capacity of more than 180 passengers, a wingspan of 35.8 meters, a length of 39.5 meters, and a height of 12.5 meters. The aircraft can fly at a cruising altitude of approximately 12,497 meters, and the maximum flight distance is about 5,680 kilometers. TAROM said that this is the first of the four Boeing 737 MAX aircraft that will enter its fleet. The plane's cruising speed reaches approximately 850 km/h, while fuel consumption and carbon emissions are up to 20% lower than those of the aircraft it replaces. At the same time, the company indicated a reduction of up to 50% in the noise footprint, while the aircraft’s windows are approximately 20% larger. Approximately two million parts are required for the assembly of a single Boeing 737 MAX. The introduction of Boeing 737 MAX aircraft is taking place in parallel with the implementation of TAROM’s restructuring plan, approved by the European Commission and with a completion deadline in December 2026. The plan provides, among other things, for the temporary limitation of the company’s network to 27 routes and the fleet to 14 aircraft until the restructuring process is completed. The company has been affected in recent years by the geopolitical context, including through the loss of certain routes, rising kerosene costs, and delays in the delivery of new aircraft, according to Economedia . The first Boeing 737 MAX 8 intended for TAROM will bear the name of Mircea Lucescu, one of the best-known Romanian coaches, who died earlier this year. The right to use the coach’s name was granted to the company by his family free of charge. “My father dedicated an entire lifetime to Romanian and European football. The fact that his name will be carried by a TAROM aircraft is a tribute that our family receives with emotion and gratitude,” declared Răzvan Lucescu. Bogdan Costaș, until recently the general director of TAROM, explained that the name is meant to associate the company with Romanian personalities who have represented the country at the international level. In 2024, the company assigned the name of Nadia Comăneci to a Boeing 737-800. The aircraft transported Romania’s delegation to the Olympic Games in Paris and continues to be used on the company’s flights. radu@romania-insider.com (Photo source: TAROM on Facebook)

data.title: Weekend calendar: Dâmbovița boat rides, Anonimul, Full Moon film festivals, Navy Day
data.description: The Open Streets program continues in Bucharest, where boat rides are part of the offer. Meanwhile audiences in Sfântu Gheorghe, in the Danube Delta, and in Biertan, in Sibiu, can enjoy a varied program of films. In Bucharest: Film Hour Until August 30 The Summer Garden of the Peasant Museum hosts a program of outdoor screenings, featuring classics and more recent public favorites. More details here . Open Streets Until October 11 For 25 weekends, the capital’s central area will host various concerts, shows, parades, workshops for children, sports activities, and guided tours. Calea Victoriei becomes pedestrian again, and, as a novelty this year, the route is extended to Ion Brezoianu Street, which is included in the program for the first time. More info here . Boat rides at Dâmbovița Apă Dulce August 14, 15 The public can enjoy free river boat rides starting at the United Nations Pier. More details here . Mihnea Dămăceanu, Dumitrița Răzlog and Theodor Pallady - Selfish Until September 6 The exhibition, hosted by Jecza și Olaru, gathers recent works by Mihnea Dămăceanu and Dumitrița Răzlog, alongside two nudes by Theodor Pallady. More here . In the country: Full Moon Horror and Fantastic Film Festival August 14 - August 16 Three days and three nights of premieres, cult films and open-air screenings in Biertan. More on the program here . Anonimul International Independent Film Festival Until August 16 This year's program includes the feature film competition, national and international short film competitions, special screenings, and Q&A sessions with filmmakers and guests. The event is held in Sfântu Gheorghe, in the Danube Delta. More details here . Romanian Navy Day August 15 The celebrations include a naval exercise in Constanța, on Romania’s Black Sea coast. More here . (Photo: Dâmbovița Delivery 2023, from organizers) editor@romania-insider.com

data.title: Romania moves to restart strategic graphite extraction at Baia de Fier
data.description: Romanian defense minister Radu Miruţă announced on Wednesday, August 12, that the graphite exploitation facility located at Baia de Fier, in Gorj County, will be reopened, with the state as the sole beneficiary of the exploitation license. The exploitation obtained the necessary approvals from the Ministries of Economy, Environment, Finance, and Justice, according to the official. “I am confident that next week at the latest, we will pass this government decision in the government meeting. The government decision is an important one because it represents the unlocking of the padlock so that the development at Baia de Fier and the exploitation of graphite can take place,” Miruţă explained . Subsequently, an international tender will be organized to prepare the pre-feasibility and feasibility studies and other necessary documentation, with the first activities estimated to begin in 2028. The European Commission approved the financing of the graphite exploitation in the sub-mountain area and extended EUR 200 million in financing for the implementation of this project. Radu Miruță emphasized that the graphite exploitation activity will bring jobs and economic development. The president of the Gorj County Council stated that he discussed with the management of the state company that will handle the extraction of graphite and received assurances that more than 100 jobs will be created, according to Profit.ro . Graphite is an increasingly sought-after mineral in modern technologies, being used, among other things, in the manufacture of conductors, as well as some essential components in mobile phones, and in the nuclear industry. Moreover, graphene, essential in green energy, is extracted from graphite, and one ton is sold for as much as EUR 200,000. Before it was shut down, the Baia de Fier factory produced 40,000 tons of graphite per year. radu@romania-insider.com (Photo source: Inquam Photos|George Calin)

data.title: Romanian president again challenges law allowing hydropower projects in protected areas
data.description: Romanian president Nicușor Dan has asked Parliament to reconsider legislation allowing the construction and completion of hydropower projects in protected areas, reopening a dispute over the balance between energy security and environmental protection. Dan submitted the request to Parliament on August 12, according to Economedia , after the Constitutional Court rejected his objections to the legislation in June. "Beyond the limits of constitutional control, we consider that the current assessment of the necessity, opportunity and efficiency of the adopted legislative solutions is required, including from the perspective of developments that have occurred since the initiation of the legislative proposal," Dan said in the note accompanying his request. The president had previously argued that the legislation could allow protected-area boundaries to be reduced and environmental assessments to be waived for entire categories of energy projects, including projects declared by the Supreme Council for National Defence to be of national security interest. The legislation, initiated by Social Democratic Party (PSD) senator Daniel Zamfir, is designed to facilitate the completion of unfinished hydropower projects. State-controlled Hidroelectrica plans to resume and complete several projects originally started during the communist period. The Energy Ministry has proposed completing around 10 unfinished hydropower plants with a combined capacity of about 700 MW, arguing that substantial investments have already been made in the projects. The projects have remained unfinished for years, with some facing environmental and legal obstacles. Their completion has gained renewed attention amid pressure to increase domestic electricity generation and strengthen Romania’s energy security. Environmental organisations, including Declic and other civic groups, oppose the resumption of some of the projects because of their potential impact on river ecosystems. They argue that upgrading existing hydropower capacity could deliver energy gains with lower environmental costs than completing older projects in protected areas. The dispute comes as Romania faces pressure on its electricity system following the shutdown of both reactors at the Cernavoda nuclear power plant because of exceptionally low Danube water levels. The government has also sought to maintain additional coal-fired generation capacity beyond existing decarbonisation deadlines. Parliament will now have to reconsider the legislation following the president’s request, despite the Constitutional Court having already ruled on its constitutionality. (Photo: Hidroelectrica) iulian@romania-insider.com
